definition_zh: 发抖；震颤；摇晃；担忧
definition_en: to shake slightly and quickly, from cold, fear, or weakness, or to shake as a thing does
core_image: 一双端着碗的手，碗里的水泛起细密的圈
scene: 雪地里，等候的人把手插进袖口，还是止不住地抖。She was trembling with cold at the bus stop.
sceneCN: 这里 tremble 是「发抖」（第 1 个义项：因寒冷、恐惧或虚弱而轻快地颤）；句意为她在公交站冻得直发抖。袖口里止不住颤的手正是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 现在分词名词化，义为「颤抖」；也可作形容词「发抖的」
同根形容词，义为「颤抖的；胆怯的」
同根名词，义为「轻微震动；颤栗」

senses.title: To shake from cold or fear
senses.definition: to shake quickly and slightly because of cold, fear, or weakness
senses.definitionCN: 因寒冷、恐惧或体弱而轻快地抖动
senses.example: His hands trembled as he opened the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 他拆信时手在发抖。
senses.why: The Latin verb tremere means to shake, and the English word keeps its plainest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 tremere 意为抖动，英语这个词保留的正是最朴素的那层意思。

senses.title: To shake with strong feeling
senses.definition: to shake because of anger, excitement, or another strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 因愤怒、激动等强烈情绪而抖
senses.example: She trembled with rage at the words.
senses.exampleCN: 听到那些话她气得发抖。
senses.why: If cold can shake a body, so can feeling, and the verb needs no new shape for it.
senses.whyCN: 寒冷能让身体抖，情绪也能，动词不必换形就能用。

senses.title: To shake, as a thing does
senses.definition: to shake slightly, said of leaves, water, or the ground
senses.definitionCN: 轻微抖动，用于树叶、水面或地面
senses.example: The leaves trembled in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 树叶在风里轻轻颤动。
senses.why: Latin used tremere of the earth as well as of limbs, so the word still covers things without a will.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语用 tremere 既指四肢也指大地，所以这个词照样管没有意志的东西。

senses.title: To be afraid of what may come
senses.definition: to feel fear or worry about something that may happen
senses.definitionCN: 对可能发生的事感到害怕或不安
senses.example: He trembled at the thought of the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 一想到考试他就心慌。
senses.why: Fear is felt in the body first, so the outward shaking comes to name the inner fear.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧先在身体上显现，于是外在的抖动就被用来指内心的害怕。

senses.title: A shaking of the body or voice
senses.definition: a slight shaking, especially of the body or the voice
senses.definitionCN: 轻度的抖动，尤指身体或嗓音
senses.example: There was a tremble in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她的嗓音里有一丝颤抖。
senses.why: The noun is simply the verb turned into a thing, naming the shaking itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词就是把这个动词变成一样东西，给抖动本身起名。

intro.en: The verb comes through French from Latin tremere, to shake, which also gave tremor and tremulous.
intro.cn: 这个动词经法语来自拉丁语 tremere（抖动），tremor 与 tremulous 同出此源。

items.en: Tremere means to shake or quake, and is used of the earth and of limbs alike.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tremere 意为抖动、震动，大地与四肢都用它。

items.en: Tremulus means trembling, and gives English tremulous.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tremulus 意为发抖的，生出英语 tremulous。

items.en: Old French trembler keeps the plain sense of shaking with cold or fear.
items.cn: 古法语 trembler 保留因寒冷或恐惧而抖的朴素义。

items.en: English borrows the verb early and uses it for both bodies and leaves.
items.cn: 英语很早就借入这个动词，既用于人，也用于树叶。

items.en: The noun form appears later, usually of the voice or the hands.
items.cn: 名词形式出现较晚，多指嗓音或手。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the trem- root of shaking, while the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of unsteady motion.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示抖动的 trem- 词根，近义组汇集其他表示不稳震动的动词。

normalIntro.en: The trem- stem turns up in tremor and tremulous, so learn it once.
normalIntro.cn: trem- 词干也出现在 tremor 与 tremulous 里，记一次就够。

normal.en: Tremere is to shake, and tremble is the plain English verb from it.
normal.cn: tremere 是抖动，tremble 就是它变来的朴素英语动词。

normal.en: Tremor is the noun for a shaking, often of the ground.
normal.cn: tremor 是抖动的名词，多指地面。

normal.en: The past tense is trembled, with -ed after the l.
normal.cn: 过去式是 trembled，l 后加 -ed。

normal.en: A tremulous voice is one that is shaking.
normal.cn: tremulous voice 就是发抖的嗓音。

normal.en: Shiver is colder, shudder is more about horror, tremble sits between.
normal.cn: shiver 更偏冷，shudder 更偏恶心，tremble 居中。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of water held by two hands that will not keep still.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手端着一杯水，怎么也拿不稳。

abstract.en: Watch the circles spread from the rim inward.
abstract.cn: 看着水纹从杯壁往里散。

abstract.en: Then let a leaf do the same thing on a bare branch.
abstract.cn: 再让一片叶子在光枝上做同样的动作。

examples.en: Her voice trembled as she read the letter aloud.
examples.cn: 她大声读信时声音在发颤。

examples.en: The old bridge trembled under the weight of the lorry.
examples.cn: 老桥在卡车的重量下颤动。

examples.en: He trembled at the thought of speaking in public.
examples.cn: 一想到公开发言他就心慌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吞不乐」——冻得吞下不开心，浑身抖个不停。

root: 拉丁语 tremere（抖动），经古法语 trembler 进入英语；同族有 tremor、tremulous

sensesIntro.en: One small, fast shaking, whether it runs through a body, a leaf, or the ground.
sensesIntro.cn: 就是一种又小又快的抖动，无论在身体里、叶子上还是地面上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands holding a cup that will not stay still.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手端着怎么也端不稳的杯子。

branches.en: The body senses, first from cold and fear, then from anger and joy.
branches.cn: 身体义：先因寒冷与恐惧，再因愤怒与激动。

branches.en: The object sense, where leaves and bridges shake too.
branches.cn: 物体义：叶子与桥也会抖。

branches.en: The inner sense, where only the feeling shakes.
branches.cn: 内心义：抖的只是那份心情。

branches.en: The noun sense, a name for the shaking itself.
branches.cn: 名词义：给这种抖动本身起名。

branches.en: The default image: cold hands at a bus stop.
branches.cn: 默认画面：车站上冻僵的手。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of shaking with a frequentative air, worn down by French.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「抖动」动词，带反复意味，经法语磨圆了形状。

latinIntro.en: Trem- stays visible in tremor and tremulous, both closer to the Latin.
latinIntro.cn: trem- 在 tremor 与 tremulous 里仍然看得见，两者都更接近拉丁原形。

items.example: The stem gives tremor and tremulous.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干生出 tremor 与 tremulous。

items.meaningCN: 经法语来自拉丁 -ulare 的动词词尾
items.example: Trem plus -ble gives tremble.
items.exampleCN: trem 加 -ble 成为 tremble。

items.example: A tremor shook the windows.
items.exampleCN: 一阵震动震得窗户直响。

items.example: She gave a tremulous smile.
items.exampleCN: 她怯怯地笑了一下。

items.example: His trembling worried the doctor.
items.exampleCN: 他的颤抖让医生担心。

items.example: The dog trembled in the rain.
items.exampleCN: 狗在雨里发抖。

items.example: The bridge trembled for a moment.
items.exampleCN: 桥颤了一下。

items.meaningCN: 构成现在分词与动名词
items.example: Tremble gives trembling.
items.exampleCN: tremble 加它成为 trembling。

definition_zh: 巨大的；极大的；极好的；了不起的
definition_en: extremely great in size, amount, or effect, or extremely good
core_image: 一面山壁横在眼前，仰头看到脖颈发酸才见顶
scene: 站在峡谷边抬头，两壁高得让人后退半步，风从下面直往上冲。The canyon drops a tremendous distance to the river.
sceneCN: 这里 tremendous 是「巨大的」（第 1 个义项：体积、数量或影响极大）；句意为峡谷到河面的落差极大。仰头看不清顶的山壁正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：极好的；了不起的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「极大地；非常」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「巨大」
同根名词，义为「震动；颤栗」

senses.title: Extremely great in size
senses.definition: very great in size, extent, or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在体积、范围或程度上非常大
senses.example: They crossed a tremendous desert.
senses.exampleCN: 他们穿过一片巨大的沙漠。
senses.why: A thing so great that one trembles at it is simply great in size, which is the direct descendant.
senses.whyCN: 大到让人发抖之物，直接就成了「体积巨大」，这是最直接的后代义。

senses.title: Extremely great in amount
senses.definition: very large in number or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 在数量上很大
senses.example: A tremendous number of people came.
senses.exampleCN: 来了极多的人。
senses.why: Number is only size counted, so the same adjective moves from space to quantity.
senses.whyCN: 数量不过是数出来的体积，所以同一个形容词从空间挪到数目上。

senses.title: Extremely strong in force
senses.definition: very strong in effect or force
senses.definitionCN: 在效力或影响上非常强
senses.example: The plan met tremendous opposition.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划遭到极大的反对。
senses.why: Force that makes people tremble is the sense closest to the Latin, applied to effect rather than body.
senses.whyCN: 让人发抖的力量最接近拉丁原义，只是作用在效果而非身体上。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: excellent or wonderful, in everyday approval
senses.definitionCN: 在日常赞许中表示「很棒」
senses.example: We had a tremendous time.
senses.exampleCN: 我们玩得非常开心。
senses.why: Weakened further, the awe becomes everyday praise for something excellent.
senses.whyCN: 再弱化一步，那份敬畏就变成对好东西的日常夸赞。

senses.title: Arousing awe or dread
senses.definition: so great as to cause wonder or fear, the oldest sense
senses.definitionCN: 大到令人惊叹或畏惧，这是最古老的义项
senses.example: The storm came on with tremendous force,
senses.exampleCN: 风暴以令人畏惧的力量袭来。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: tremendus names what must be trembled at.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：tremendus 指的就是「必须对它发抖」之物。

intro.en: The word is Latin tremendus, to be trembled at, from tremere, to tremble.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语 tremendus，意为「令人发抖的」，出自动词 tremere（发抖）。

items.en: Tremere means to tremble, and tremendus is the thing one must tremble at.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tremere 意为发抖，tremendus 就是「必须对它发抖」之物。

items.en: The Latin gerundive ending -ndus marks something that ought to be feared or done.
items.cn: 拉丁动形词词尾 -ndus 标记「应该被畏惧或应做」之物。

items.en: English first uses the word for things that inspire awe and dread.
items.cn: 英语最初用这个词指引起敬畏与恐惧的事物。

items.en: In the nineteenth century it weakens into a general word for very great.
items.cn: 十九世纪它弱化为泛指「非常大」的词。

items.en: Recent usage adds an everyday sense of very good.
items.cn: 近期用法又添上「非常好」的日常义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the trem- root of trembling, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for very large.
note.cn: 形近组共用 trem-（发抖）词根，近义组汇集表示极大的其他词。

definition_en: a small involuntary shaking of the body, or a slight quivering of the ground, a voice or a machine
core_image: 一只手平放在桌面上，指尖却在细密地抖动，桌面落着一层薄薄的灰
scene: 深夜的地震观测室里，纸带记录仪忽然划出一小段密集的锯齿。 A faint tremor rattled the instruments on the shelf just after midnight.
sceneCN: 这里 tremor 是名词「微震、轻微地震」（第 1 个义项：规模较小、常成串出现的地震）；句意为午夜刚过，一次微弱的地震让架上的仪器轻轻震动。

senses.title: A small earthquake
senses.definition: a small earthquake, especially one of many that follow or precede a larger shock
senses.definitionCN: 规模较小的地震，尤指主震前后成串出现的余震或前震
senses.example: A series of tremors followed the main shock.
senses.exampleCN: 主震之后跟着一连串微震。
senses.why: Latin tremor named any trembling at all; seismology narrowed the word to small shocks that are clearly weaker than the main earthquake.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 tremor 本指任何颤抖；地震学把这个词收窄为明显弱于主震的小震。

senses.title: Involuntary shaking of the body
senses.definition: an involuntary, rhythmic shaking of part of the body, often caused by a neurological disorder or by a drug
senses.definitionCN: 身体某部分不由自主、有节律地抖动，常由神经系统疾病或药物引起
senses.example: The new medication reduced the tremor in his hands.
senses.exampleCN: 新药减轻了他双手的震颤。
senses.why: medicine kept the oldest sense of the Latin noun and made it clinical: a tremor is shaking the patient cannot stop.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了这一拉丁名词最古老的意义并使之临床化：震颤是病人止不住的抖动。

senses.title: A quaver from emotion
senses.titleCN: 情绪引起的手或声音发抖
senses.definition: a slight shaking of the hands or voice caused by fear, cold, anger or excitement
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧、寒冷、愤怒或激动而出现的手部或声音的轻微发抖
senses.example: She answered with a slight tremor in her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 她回答时声音微微发颤。
senses.why: the physical sense extends to the voice because the same muscles that shake the hand also shake the throat.
senses.whyCN: 这一身体义能扩展到声音，是因为让手发抖的肌肉同样会让喉咙发抖。

senses.title: A slight shaking of the ground
senses.definition: a faint shaking of the ground that is weaker than a real earthquake, as from traffic, blasting or a distant quake
senses.definitionCN: 比真正地震更弱的地面抖动，可来自车辆、爆破或远处的地震
senses.example: A passing train sent a tremor through the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆过路的火车让地板传来一阵颤动。
senses.why: once the noun meant any shaking, it was natural to use it for ground movement that is felt but does not qualify as an earthquake.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个名词本指任何抖动，用它来表示「能感觉到但算不上地震」的地面运动就很自然。

senses.title: Volcanic tremor
senses.definition: a continuous rhythmic ground vibration at a volcano, generated by the movement of magma or hydrothermal fluids
senses.definitionCN: 火山处持续的、有节律的地面振动，由岩浆或热液流体的运动产生
senses.example: Harmonic tremor often precedes an eruption.
senses.exampleCN: 谐波颤动常常出现在喷发之前。
senses.why: volcanology needed a word for shaking that lasts minutes to hours, unlike the sharp jolt of a tectonic quake, and borrowed the medical-seismic noun.
senses.whyCN: 火山学需要一个词指持续数分钟到数小时的抖动，以区别于构造地震的骤然一震，于是借用了这个兼有医学与地震含义的名词。

senses.title: A quaver in music or speech
senses.definition: a rapid, slight fluctuation of pitch in a singing voice or in the sound of an instrument
senses.definitionCN: 歌声或乐器声中音高快速而轻微的起伏
senses.example: The singer's tremor added warmth to the long final note.
senses.exampleCN: 歌手那一点颤抖让结尾的长音更有温度。
senses.why: the emotional quaver of sense three becomes a deliberate expressive device when a performer controls it.
senses.whyCN: 第三个义项里情绪性的颤抖，一旦被表演者控制，就成了有意的表现手段。

senses.title: Mild social or political unrest
senses.titleCN: 社会或政治的轻微动荡
senses.definition: a slight wave of unrest or anxiety passing through a group, institution or society
senses.definitionCN: 在群体、机构或社会中掠过的一阵轻微不安或动荡
senses.example: Tremors of discontent ran through the party after the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 投票之后，不满的微澜掠过整个政党。
senses.why: the image of a body shaking without falling apart fits a society that is disturbed but not yet broken.
senses.whyCN: 身体抖动却尚未散架的意象，正好对应一个受到扰动但还未破裂的社会。

senses.title: Sustained mechanical or acoustic vibration
senses.titleCN: 声学或机械的持续振动
senses.definition: a continuous low-level vibration measured in a machine, a structure or a sound field
senses.definitionCN: 在机器、结构或声场中被测量到的持续低频振动
senses.example: Engineers measured the tremor of the turbine housing.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师测量了涡轮外壳的持续振动。
senses.why: engineering uses the word for unwanted steady shaking that is weaker than a fault but still tells a story about wear.
senses.whyCN: 工程上用这个词指不受欢迎的稳定抖动，它比故障轻，却仍然透露磨损的信息。

intro.en: Tremor comes from Latin tremor, a trembling, a noun built on the verb tremere, to tremble or quake. It entered English in the fourteenth century through medical writing and later acquired seismic, musical and engineering senses.
intro.cn: tremor 来自拉丁 tremor「颤抖」，是建于动词 tremere「发抖、震动」之上的名词。该词于十四世纪经医学著作进入英语，后来又发展出地震、音乐与工程方面的义项。

items.en: Tremere meant to shake, quake or tremble with fear. It is the verb behind the whole English family, including tremble, tremulous and tremendous.
items.cn: tremere 意为「震动、发抖、因恐惧而颤抖」。它是整个英语同族词的动词来源，包括「发抖」「颤抖的」与「令人发抖的」诸词。

items.en: Tremor was the noun of state, the trembling itself rather than the act of starting to tremble; English took the noun, not the verb.
items.cn: tremor 是状态名词，指颤抖本身，而不是「开始发抖」的动作；英语借入的是名词，而非动词。

items.en: Tremulus meant trembling and gave English tremulous. The gerundive tremendus, to be trembled at, gave tremendous, whose modern sense of huge is a later weakening of dreadful.
items.cn: tremulus 意为「颤抖的」，衍生出英语中表示「颤抖的」形容词。动名词 tremendus 意为「令人发抖的」，衍生出表示「巨大的」形容词，其现代「庞大」义是「可怕」义的后期弱化。

items.en: The everyday verb tremble came through Old French trembler, generally considered a development of Latin tremulare from tremulus rather than a direct borrowing of tremere.
items.cn: 日常动词「发抖」经古法语而来，一般认为是拉丁 tremulare（出自 tremulus）的发展，而非直接借自 tremere。

items.en: Medical texts fixed tremor as the clinical name for involuntary shaking. Seismology then used it for small shocks, and twentieth-century volcanology added volcanic tremor for continuous volcanic shaking.
items.cn: 医学文献把 tremor 固定为不自主颤抖的临床名称。地震学随后用它指小震，二十世纪的火山学又加上了「火山颤动」这一搭配，指持续的火山抖动。

items.en: Two tiers of doubt: the first date of the seismic sense is only approximate, a dating question; the deeper root of tremere is usually reconstructed as an Indo-European trembling stem, which is a reconstruction and not a recorded form, a root question.
items.cn: 来源不确定，分两档：地震义的首见年代只是约数，属年代存疑；tremere 更深的词根通常被重构为一个印欧语「发抖」词干，属重构形式而非有记录的形式，属词根存疑。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin trembling stock; group two holds near neighbours that name other kinds of shaking.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「发抖」词干的词；第二组是同样表示抖动的近义词。

entries.definition: To shake with small rapid movements, usually from fear, cold or weakness; it is the plain verb where tremor is the clinical noun.
entries.definitionCN: 以细小的快速动作抖动，通常因恐惧、寒冷或虚弱；tremble 是日常动词，tremor 则是临床名词。

entries.definition: Shaking slightly, or showing such shaking, as a tremulous voice or a tremulous smile.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微颤抖的，或显出这种颤抖的，如发颤的声音或怯怯的微笑。

entries.definition: From the Latin gerundive meaning to be trembled at; English shifted it from dreadful to simply enormous.
entries.definitionCN: 来自意为「令人发抖」的拉丁动名词；英语把「可怕」义转为单纯的「巨大」。

entries.definition: A musical effect of rapid repeated notes or a wavering tone, borrowed from Italian, where the Latin root kept its shaking sense.
entries.definitionCN: 由快速重复的音或摇摆的音色构成的音乐效果，借自意大利语，那里拉丁词根仍保留抖动义。

entries.definition: A sudden convulsive shaking of the whole body, often from horror or cold; it is stronger and briefer than a tremor.
entries.definitionCN: 全身突然的痉挛式抖动，常因恐惧或寒冷；比 tremor 更强烈也更短促。

entries.definition: To shake violently, used both of the earth and of a person's limbs; the noun form is the short word for an earthquake.
entries.definitionCN: 剧烈抖动，既用于大地也用于人的四肢；其名词形式是「地震」的简短说法。

entries.definition: A rapid alternation of position about a rest point; it is the physical pattern of which a tremor is one felt instance.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕静止位置快速往复运动；它是物理模式，tremor 则是一次被感觉到的实例。

entries.definition: A slight, fine trembling, as of a leaf in wind or a lip before tears; it is softer and more delicate than tremor.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微细密的抖动，如风中的叶子或落泪前的嘴唇；比 tremor 更轻柔细微。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin stem, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词干、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: trem- is the shaking stem: Latin tremere shook, and tremor is the shaking itself.
normal.cn: trem- 是「抖」的词干：拉丁 tremere 是发抖，tremor 就是那阵抖动本身。

normal.en: The family splits by part of speech: a noun, a daily verb, an adjective of shaking and a musical noun.
normal.cn: 同族按词性分流：一个名词、一个日常动词、一个表示颤抖的形容词与一个音乐名词。

normal.en: Earth tremor is the mildest seismic word; earthquake names the full event.
normal.cn: 「地面颤动」是最轻的地震说法，「地震」则指完整事件。

normal.en: Medical texts pair tremor with intention, rest and posture, the three situations that change how it appears.
normal.cn: 医学文献把震颤与意向、静止、姿势三种情形搭配，因为它们会改变震颤的表现。

normal.en: A tremor in the voice is the body's shaking heard through sound.
normal.cn: 声音里的颤抖，就是身体的抖动被听见。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of water on a train table, its surface never quite still.
abstract.cn: 想象列车小桌上的一杯水，水面始终静不下来。

abstract.en: Picture a singer whose last note wobbles like a plucked wire.
abstract.cn: 想象一位歌手，最后一个音像被拨动的金属丝一样摇摆。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone speaks calmly but no one meets anyone's eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子里人人语气平静，却没有人对上彼此的目光。

examples.en: The first tremor came before dawn and lasted only a few seconds.
examples.cn: 第一次微震在天亮前到来，只持续了几秒钟。

examples.en: His hand showed a fine tremor when he tried to write.
examples.cn: 他想写字时，手出现细密的颤抖。

examples.en: Volcanic tremor is continuous, unlike the sharp jolt of a tectonic quake.
examples.cn: 火山颤动是持续的，不像构造地震那样骤然一震。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「trem（抖）+ or」——手一直抖，地轻轻颤 → 震颤、微震、颤音

root: 拉丁 tremere「发抖、震动」的名词形式 tremor「颤抖」；同族另有形容词 tremulus「颤抖的」与动名词 tremendus「令人发抖的」，经法语还派生出日常动词「发抖」一支。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one sensation: a fine shaking too weak to break anything. It starts in the body, moves to the voice, then to the ground, then narrows into a small quake, a volcanic signal, a social mood and a machine reading.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种感觉展开：一种细密、弱到不足以弄断任何东西的抖动。它从身体出发，转到声音，再到地面，随后收窄为小震、火山信号、社会情绪与机器读数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fine rapid shaking that never grows into a full break.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种细密快速的抖动，始终没有发展成彻底的断裂。

branches.en: BODY AND EMOTION: the original human shaking, caused by nerves or by feeling.
branches.cn: 身体与情绪：最初的人身抖动，由神经或情绪引起。

branches.en: VOICE: the same shaking made audible, then controlled as expression.
branches.cn: 声音：同一种抖动被听见，随后被控制成表现手段。

branches.en: GROUND: shaking felt in the earth, first as a slight movement, then as a small quake.
branches.cn: 地面：在大地上感到的抖动，先是轻微运动，再成为小震。

branches.en: VOLCANO: a continuous signal that magma is moving and pressure is building.
branches.cn: 火山：岩浆在移动、压力在积累时发出的持续信号。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: the same weak, steady shaking read into a society or a machine.
branches.cn: 系统：同一种微弱而稳定的抖动被读进社会或机器之中。

intro.en: Tremor is a Latin noun of state built directly on a verb, and its stem recurs in adjectives, a verb and an Italian musical borrowing.
intro.cn: tremor 是直接建于动词之上的拉丁状态名词，其词干在形容词、动词与一个意大利语音乐借词中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin tremere, tremor, tremulus and tremendus underlie tremor, tremulous, tremendous and tremolo.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tremere、tremor、tremulus 与 tremendus 构成本词及「颤抖的」「令人发抖的」「颤音」等同族词。

items.example: The stem trem- names the shaking itself.
items.exampleCN: 词干 trem- 直接指抖动本身。

items.example: Tremor is the state of trembling.
items.exampleCN: 这个词指的就是「正在发抖」的状态。

items.example: The tremor lasted a few seconds.
items.exampleCN: 那次微震持续了几秒钟。

items.example: Her tremulous voice betrayed her nerves.
items.exampleCN: 她颤抖的声音泄露了紧张。

items.meaningCN: 令人发抖的，后转指巨大
items.example: A tremendous roar came from the crater.
items.exampleCN: 火山口传来一声令人震骇的轰鸣。

items.structure: Old French trembler, generally considered from Latin tremulare
items.example: Her hands tremble in the cold.
items.exampleCN: 她的双手在寒冷中发抖。

items.example: The strings played a soft tremolo.
items.exampleCN: 弦乐奏出一段柔和的颤音。

items.meaningCN: 颤动的；管风琴颤音音栓
items.example: The organ's tremulant swelled the final chord.
items.exampleCN: 管风琴的颤音音栓让结尾和弦饱满起来。

items.example: She tremulously asked whether the quake was over.
items.exampleCN: 她声音发颤地问地震是否过去了。

definition_zh: 沟；壕沟；战壕；海沟；挖沟
definition_en: a long, narrow, deep cut in the ground, a military ditch, or a deep depression on the ocean floor; also to dig such a cut
core_image: 地面被直直切出一条窄而深的槽，两侧的土堆成整齐的脊
scene: 工人在路面上开出一条窄槽，准备埋电缆。 Workers dug a narrow trench along the curb for the new cable.
sceneCN: 这里 trench 指「人工挖出的狭长沟槽」（第 1 个义项：为工程开挖的沟）；句意为工人们沿路缘挖出一条窄沟，用来埋新电缆。图中可辨识物件：路缘、窄沟、铁锹、电缆盘。

pos.zh: 沟；壕沟；战壕；海沟；沟状凹陷

derivatives.zh: 使扎根；用壕沟防护
巩固；壕沟工事
尖锐的；有力的（同源但词义分化）
风衣
堑壕战

senses.title: A dug ditch
senses.definition: a long, narrow cut dug in the ground for drainage, cables or foundations
senses.definitionCN: 为排水、电缆或基础而在地面挖出的狭长深沟
senses.example: Workers dug a narrow trench along the curb for the new cable.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们沿路缘挖出一条窄沟，用来埋新电缆。
senses.why: trench goes back to Old French trenchier 'to cut', so the noun starts as the line left by a cutting action.
senses.whyCN: trench 上溯到古法语 trenchier「切」，因此这个名词最初就是切割动作留下的那条线。

senses.title: A military trench
senses.definition: a long defensive ditch from which soldiers fight and shelter
senses.definitionCN: 士兵据以作战与隐蔽的狭长防御沟
senses.example: The regiment held the trench through the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个团在战壕里守了一整个冬天。
senses.why: the military sense narrows the engineering sense to a ditch that protects bodies from fire.
senses.whyCN: 军事义把工程义收窄为一条保护身体免受火力的沟。

senses.title: A deep ocean trench
senses.definition: a long, narrow, very deep depression on the ocean floor
senses.definitionCN: 洋底上狭长而极深的凹陷
senses.example: The earthquake epicentre lay near a deep ocean trench.
senses.exampleCN: 震中位于一条深海沟附近。
senses.why: the ocean floor has cuts of the same narrow shape, so geology reused the word for them.
senses.whyCN: 洋底也有同样狭长形状的切口，因此地质学沿用了这个词。

senses.title: A geological trough
senses.definition: a long, narrow depression in rock or sediment formed by faulting or erosion
senses.definitionCN: 由断裂或侵蚀在岩石、沉积物中形成的狭长凹陷
senses.example: A fault trench runs across the valley floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一条断层沟横穿谷底。
senses.why: the shape, not the digging, is what matters here: a natural cut in the ground is still a trench.
senses.whyCN: 这里重要的是形状而非挖掘：地面上的天然切口仍叫 trench。

senses.title: To dig a ditch
senses.definition: to dig a long, narrow cut in the ground
senses.definitionCN: 在地面挖出狭长的沟
senses.example: They trenched the field to drain the low corner.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在田里挖沟，为低洼的一角排水。
senses.why: the verb is simply the action that produces the noun, and English often pairs such nouns with a zero-derived verb.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是产生这个名词的动作，英语常让这类名词与零派生动词配对。

senses.title: To cut a trench through land
senses.titleCN: 动词：在土地上开槽穿过
senses.definition: to cut a trench across or through an area, as for a pipeline
senses.definitionCN: 为铺设管道等而在某区域横切出一条沟
senses.example: Crews trenched the hillside for the water main.
senses.exampleCN: 施工队在坡上开沟，铺设供水主管。
senses.why: with an object like field or hillside, the verb stresses the area crossed rather than the ditch itself.
senses.whyCN: 接 field 或 hillside 这类宾语时，动词强调的是被穿越的区域，而非沟本身。

senses.title: To open an excavation trench
senses.definition: to open a controlled excavation cut at an archaeological site
senses.definitionCN: 在考古遗址上开挖有控制的探沟
senses.example: The team trenched the mound in a grid pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 团队按网格在土丘上开挖探沟。
senses.why: archaeology adopted the engineering word for its own orderly cuts through layered ground.
senses.whyCN: 考古学借用了工程词，指它在层状地面上开出的有序切口。

senses.title: Archaic: to encroach
senses.definition: to encroach or infringe upon something, as in the old phrase trench upon
senses.definitionCN: 侵占或侵犯某物，见于旧短语 trench upon
senses.example: The old statute forbade anyone to trench upon the commons.
senses.exampleCN: 旧法令禁止任何人侵占公地。
senses.why: the image of cutting into another's ground produced an older legal sense of encroachment that survives only in archaic prose.
senses.whyCN: 切入他人土地的意象产生了较早的法律义「侵占」，今仅存于古旧文字。

intro.en: Trench comes from Old French trenche 'a cut, ditch', from trenchier 'to cut', a verb of uncertain deeper origin, sometimes linked to Latin truncare 'to cut off'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: trench 来自古法语 trenche「切口、沟」，出自 trenchier「切」；这个动词更深的来源不确定，有人把它与拉丁 truncare「切掉」联系起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trenchier meant 'to cut, slice, carve'. Its relation to Latin truncare 'to cut off' is often proposed but not established beyond doubt.
items.cn: trenchier 意为「切、割、刻」。人们常提出它与拉丁 truncare「切掉」有关，但并未确凿证实。

items.en: The noun trenche named a cut or a ditch, and English borrowed it in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 trenche 指切口或沟，英语在十五世纪借入。

items.en: From the seventeenth century trench was used for siege and field fortifications, and the sense dominated after the trench warfare of 1914 to 1918.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，trench 用于攻城与野战工事；一九一四至一九一八年的堑壕战之后，这一义项占据主导。

items.en: Oceanography applied the word to deep linear depressions of the sea floor in the late nineteenth century.
items.cn: 海洋学在十九世纪末把这个词用于洋底狭长的深凹陷。

items.en: The verb meaning 'to dig a trench' developed alongside the noun; the archaic sense 'to encroach' is older and now rare.
items.cn: 意为「挖沟」的动词与名词并行发展；古旧的「侵占」义更早，今已罕见。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether trenchier descends from Latin truncare is disputed, and the exact first English date is not fixed, so any intermediate form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：trenchier 是否源自拉丁 truncare 尚有争议，英语最早书证的确切年代也未固定，凡给出的中间形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one separates trench from its own compounds and its sharp-edged relative trenchant; group two holds near synonyms for a long cut or channel.
note.cn: 第一组把 trench 与其复合词、以及同源但词义分化的 trenchant 分开；第二组是表示狭长切口或通道的近义词。

entries.definition: En- 'in' plus trench: to fix firmly, or to protect with a trench; it is a verb, not the ditch itself.
entries.definitionCN: en-「进入」加 trench：使牢固扎根，或用壕沟防护；它是动词，不指沟本身。

entries.definition: From the same Old French 'cutting' stock: sharp and forceful in speech or writing, not a physical ditch.
entries.definitionCN: 同出古法语「切」的词源：指言辞犀利有力，并非实体沟渠。

entries.definition: A belted raincoat named after the trenches of the First World War; it contains trench but names clothing.
entries.definitionCN: 得名于第一次世界大战战壕的束带雨衣；它虽含 trench，却指衣物。

entries.definition: War fought from opposing systems of trenches; it uses trench but names a kind of conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 从相互对峙的壕沟体系进行的战争；它虽含 trench，却指一种冲突形式。

entries.definition: A long narrow channel dug for drainage or irrigation; it is usually shallower and less military than a trench.
entries.definitionCN: 为排水或灌溉挖出的狭长渠道；通常比 trench 浅，也没有军事含义。

entries.definition: A passage for water, natural or built; it stresses flow rather than the cut itself.
entries.definitionCN: 天然或人工的水道；强调水流，而非切口本身。

entries.definition: A long narrow depression cut into a surface, often shallow and machined; a trench is deeper and in ground.
entries.definitionCN: 切在表面上的狭长凹槽，常较浅且为机加工；trench 更深且开在地面。

entries.definition: A narrow cut made by a plough in soil; it is agricultural and shallow, not a fortification.
entries.definitionCN: 犁在土里开出的狭沟；属农业用途且较浅，不是工事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: trench- 'cut' + the noun ending: the cut itself.
normal.cn: trench-「切」+ 名词词尾：切出来的那道口子。

normal.en: The family runs trench, entrench, entrenchment, trenchant, trench coat.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 trench、entrench、entrenchment、trenchant、trench coat。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the military sense: trench warfare, trench coat, trench foot.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出军事义：堑壕战、风衣、战壕足。

normal.en: Geology says trench for the deep cut and trench for its two walls.
normal.cn: 地质学用 trench 指深切口，也指切口的两壁。

normal.en: The verb takes field or line as its object: trench a field, trench a line.
normal.cn: 这个动词常以 field 或 line 作宾语：在田里开沟、沿线开沟。

abstract.en: Picture a cake cut once and left open, its layers exposed on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蛋糕被切了一刀后摊开，两边的层次都露出来。

abstract.en: Picture two gardens separated by a line no one is allowed to cross.
abstract.cn: 想象两座花园之间隔着一条谁也不许越过的线。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that cuts cleanly through an argument.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话干净利落地切开一场争论。

examples.en: The workers filled the trench after laying the pipe.
examples.cn: 铺好管道后，工人把沟填了回去。

examples.en: Soldiers shared a narrow trench for three weeks.
examples.cn: 士兵们在一条窄战壕里共处了三周。

examples.en: The Mariana Trench is the deepest known ocean trench.
examples.cn: 马里亚纳海沟是已知最深的洋底海沟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「trench（切）」——在地上切出一道窄口 → 沟、战壕、海沟

root: 古法语 trenche「切口、沟」来自 trenchier「切」；与拉丁 truncare「切掉」的联系常被提出但未确证，更深来源不确定，相关中间形式均属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one cut: a dug ditch, a military line, an ocean deep, a fault trough, three kinds of digging, and an archaic encroachment that survives in old prose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一条切口展开：挖出的沟、军事防线、海底深凹、断层沟、三种开挖动作，以及仅存于古旧文字的侵占义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single straight cut opening the ground into two walls.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道笔直的切口把地面分成两壁。

branches.en: CUT IN GROUND: a dug ditch and a natural fault trough share the shape.
branches.cn: 地面切口：人工沟与天然断层沟共享同一形状。

branches.en: DEFENSIVE LINE: the ditch becomes a place to fight from.
branches.cn: 防御线：沟变成据以作战的地方。

branches.en: OCEANIC CUT: the same narrow deep shape lies under the sea.
branches.cn: 海底切口：同样的狭长深形出现在海面之下。

branches.en: DIGGING ACTS: engineering, crossing land, archaeology.
branches.cn: 开挖动作：工程、穿越土地、考古。

branches.en: OLD INFRINGEMENT: cutting into another's ground became legal encroachment.
branches.cn: 旧日侵占：切入他人土地变成法律上的侵占。

intro.en: Trench is a borrowed French noun of cutting; its family includes the verb entrench, the adjective trenchant and two modern compounds.
intro.cn: trench 是借自法语的「切」名词；其词族包括动词 entrench、形容词 trenchant 与两个现代复合词。

latinIntro.en: The deeper origin is uncertain; a link to Latin truncare 'to cut off' is often proposed but not proven, so the Latin entries are given only as possible sources.
latinIntro.cn: 更深来源不确定；与拉丁 truncare「切掉」的联系常被提出却未证实，因此所给拉丁条目只能视为可能的来源。

items.example: The verb named the act of cutting into the ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指切入地面的动作。

items.example: The trench was two metres deep.
items.exampleCN: 这条沟有两米深。

items.example: They trenched the whole field.
items.exampleCN: 他们给整块田开了沟。

items.meaning: to fix firmly; to fortify with trenches
items.meaningCN: 使牢固扎根；用壕沟防护
items.example: The habit was entrenched by years of use.
items.exampleCN: 这个习惯因多年使用而根深蒂固。

items.meaning: a fortified ditch; a fixed state
items.meaningCN: 壕沟工事；根深蒂固的状态
items.example: The entrenchment slowed the advance.
items.exampleCN: 壕沟工事拖慢了推进。

items.meaningCN: 切割的；引申为犀利有力的
items.example: Her trenchant criticism silenced the room.
items.exampleCN: 她犀利的批评让全场安静。

items.meaning: a belted raincoat in military style
items.example: He wore a trench coat in the rain.
items.exampleCN: 他雨天穿着一件风衣。

items.meaning: war fought from opposing trench systems
items.meaningCN: 以对峙壕沟体系进行的战争
items.example: Trench warfare defined the western front.
items.exampleCN: 堑壕战定义了西线战场。

latinEntries.structure: truncare, truncavi, truncatum (verb, first conjugation; possible source)
truncus, trunci (m., second declension; possible source)

definition_zh: 趋势；倾向；潮流；走向
definition_en: a general direction in which something is developing or changing over time
core_image: 纸上一条折线慢慢向上爬，旁边标着几个年份
scene: 办公室里，分析师把几年的销量画成折线，线在最后一段明显上扬。The trend in sales has been upward for three years.
sceneCN: 这里 trend 是「趋势；走向」（第 1 个义项：事物随时间发展的总方向）；句意为销量的走势三年来一直在上升。纸上那条慢慢上扬的折线，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 trend 加 -y 构成，义为「时髦的；赶潮流的」
由 trend 与 setter 复合，义为「引领潮流的人」
由 trend 加 -ing 构成，义为「正在流行的」

senses.title: The line on the graph
senses.definition: the general direction in which a situation is moving over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 情况在一段时间内发展的总方向
senses.example: The trend in sales has been upward for three years.
senses.exampleCN: 销量的走势三年来一直在上升。
senses.why: The word began as a turning of a river or a coast, and a line that keeps turning one way became a trend.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指河流或海岸的转弯，而一直朝一边转的线就成了趋势。

senses.title: What everyone is doing
senses.definition: a fashion or habit that many people take up at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 许多人同时接受的时髦做法
senses.example: Short jackets are the trend this autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 短外套是今年秋天的潮流。
senses.why: When many people turn the same way at once, the direction looks like a fashion to follow.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人同时转向同一个方向，这个方向看起来就像可以追随的风尚。

senses.title: Leaning in one direction
senses.definition: to move or develop generally in a stated direction
senses.definitionCN: 大体朝某个方向移动或发展
senses.example: Prices trended downward through the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 整个夏天价格趋于下降。
senses.why: The verb keeps the oldest picture: a course that keeps bending the same way.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留了最古老的画面：一条一直朝同一方向弯的走向。

senses.title: Turning away from a fashion
senses.definition: to move away from a popular style in a new direction
senses.definitionCN: 离开流行样式，转向新的方向
senses.example: Designers are turning away from bright colours this year.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师今年正逐渐远离鲜亮的颜色。
senses.why: The verb keeps the old idea of a course bending, and fashion courses bend too.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词保留着航线折弯的旧意，时尚的走向同样会折弯。

intro.en: Trend first named the turning of a coastline or a river, and only later the direction of a set of figures.
intro.cn: trend 最初指海岸线或河流的转弯，后来才指一组数字的方向。

items.en: The verb trendan meant to turn or revolve, close to the modern tr-, dr- turn family.
items.cn: 古英语动词 trendan 意为转动、旋转，与表示「转」的词族相近。

items.en: A trend was the curve of a shore or the bend of a river.
items.cn: 中古英语里 trend 指海岸的弧线或河流的弯处。

items.en: Sailors spoke of the trend of a coast as its general direction.
items.cn: 水手用 the trend of a coast 指海岸的大致走向。

items.en: Statistics borrowed the word for the general direction of changing numbers.
items.cn: 统计学借用这个词，指变化中的数字的总方向。

items.en: Twentieth-century magazines applied it to fashion, giving the sense of a popular style.
items.cn: 二十世纪的杂志把它用在时尚上，产生了流行风潮的含义。

note.en: The first group shares the trend stem, the second holds other words for direction and fashion.
note.cn: 第一组共享 trend 词干，第二组收其他表示方向与流行的词。

entries.definition: Very fashionable.
entries.definitionCN: 时髦的

entries.definition: Currently popular online.
entries.definitionCN: 正在走红的

entries.definition: A person who starts a fashion.
entries.definitionCN: 引领潮流者

entries.definition: A leaning toward a kind of behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向

entries.definition: A popular style at a given time.
entries.definitionCN: 时尚；风尚

entries.definition: The line along which something moves.
entries.definitionCN: 方向

normalIntro.en: Trend is a short word for a long line: the way things have been going and are likely to keep going.
normalIntro.cn: trend 是个短词，说的是长线：事情一路走来的方向，以及大概会继续走下去的方向。

normal.en: The verb is the same word: prices trend up.
normal.cn: 动词形式一模一样：prices trend up。

normal.en: The adjective trendy cuts the d and adds y.
normal.cn: 形容词 trendy 去掉 d 再加 y。

normal.en: A trendsetter sets the trend for others to follow.
normal.cn: trendsetter 设下潮流让旁人跟随。

normal.en: The plural is simply trends.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：trends。

normal.en: Statistics made the word famous: a trend line on a chart.
normal.cn: 统计学让这个词流行：图表上的一条趋势线。

abstract.en: A coastline bending the same way for miles.
abstract.cn: 海岸线绵延数里朝同一方向弯。

abstract.en: Water finding one slope and staying with it.
abstract.cn: 水找到一面斜坡，就一路顺着它。

abstract.en: Many people turning their heads at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 许多人同时把头转向同一个方向。

examples.en: There is a clear trend toward smaller cars in the city.
examples.cn: 这座城市明显有偏爱小车的趋势。

examples.en: Rents in the old quarter have trended upward since spring.
examples.cn: 老城区的租金自春天以来趋于上涨。

examples.en: She never follows the fashion of the season.
examples.cn: 她从不追随当季的风尚。

dict_mnemonic.text: trend 里的 tren 一念就像「转」——大家往一个方向转，就成了潮流。

root: 古英语 trendan（转动），中古英语指海岸或河流的弯向，近代经统计学与时尚用语扩展为「趋势、潮流」；同族词有 trendy、trendsetter、trending。

sensesIntro.en: First the direction of a changing figure, then the fashion many follow, then the verb for moving that way.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是变化数字的方向，再是众人追随的时髦，最后是朝那个方向走的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bending line on a chart.
core.cn: 核心意象：图表上弯曲的线。

branches.en: The figure branch: numbers moving one way.
branches.cn: 数字分支：数字朝一个方向走。

branches.en: The fashion branch: many people turning together.
branches.cn: 时尚分支：许多人一起转向。

branches.en: The action branch: a course leaning one way.
branches.cn: 动作分支：走势朝一边倾。

branches.en: The chart branch: both are read on a line.
branches.cn: 图表分支：两者都在一条线上读出。

branches.en: The crowd branch: a habit becomes a general direction.
branches.cn: 人群分支：一种习惯变成总方向。

intro.en: Trend is a short Germanic stem that now builds compounds and derivatives in business and fashion.
intro.cn: trend 是短小的日耳曼语词干，如今在商业与时尚领域构成复合词与派生词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is not Latin; the Latin words below are cousins through shared Indo-European roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干并非拉丁语；下面的拉丁词只是通过共同印欧词根构成的远亲。

items.example: The stem works as noun and verb alike.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干既可作名词也可作动词。

items.example: It forms trendy, full of fashion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trendy，满身时尚的。

items.example: It forms trending, popular right now.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trending，眼下正走红的。

items.example: The two words say what the person does.
items.exampleCN: 两个词直接说出这个人做的事。

items.example: Up names the direction of the line.
items.exampleCN: up 指明线的走向。

items.example: Down names the opposite direction.
items.exampleCN: down 指明相反的方向。

items.example: The line makes the direction visible.
items.exampleCN: 这条线让方向看得见。

items.example: Several trends appeared at once.
items.exampleCN: 数个趋势同时出现。

definition_zh: 试验；试用；审判；审讯
definition_en: a test of something to see whether it works, or the formal hearing of a case in a court
core_image: 一辆贴着彩条的车在试验场上绕圈，工程师盯着屏幕记数据
scene: 试验场上有一辆涂着彩条的车，工程师坐在场边的帐篷里看屏幕。The new engine is still on trial before it goes on sale.
sceneCN: 这里 trial 是「试验；试用」（第 1 个义项：为检验效果而进行的测试）；句意为这款新发动机在上市前仍在试用测试中。贴着彩条在场上绕圈的车，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: trial 的词根，义为「尝试；审判」
由 try 与 out 复合，义为「选拔；试用」
由 try 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恼火的；艰难的」

senses.title: The test run
senses.definition: an act of testing something over a period to see how well it works
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内测试某物效果如何的行为
senses.example: The new engine is still on trial before it goes on sale.
senses.exampleCN: 这款新发动机在上市前仍在试用测试中。
senses.why: The ending -al turns the verb try into a noun, and the oldest sense is the testing of something.
senses.whyCN: -al 后缀把动词 try 变为名词，最古老的含义就是检验某物。

senses.title: The day in court
senses.definition: the formal examination of a case by a judge and often a jury
senses.definitionCN: 由法官及常设陪审团对案件进行的正式审理
senses.example: The trial lasted three weeks and ended with a verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 这场审判持续了三周，以裁决结束。
senses.why: A court also tests the facts of a case, so the legal hearing borrowed the same word as the engine test.
senses.whyCN: 法庭同样在检验案件的事实，于是庭审与发动机测试共用了同一个词。

senses.title: A hard testing time
senses.definition: a person or situation that tests your patience or strength
senses.definitionCN: 考验人耐心或承受力的人或处境
senses.example: Looking after three children alone was a real trial.
senses.exampleCN: 独自照料三个孩子真是一场考验。
senses.why: Anything that puts you under pressure is testing you, so hard days wear the same label.
senses.whyCN: 任何给你压力的事都在检验你，于是艰难的日子也挂上同一种标签。

senses.title: The person who is tested
senses.definition: a person taking part in a test to be chosen for a team or a job
senses.definitionCN: 参加测试以争取进入队伍或获得职位的人
senses.example: Three new players were on trial with the club in July.
senses.exampleCN: 七月有三名新球员在俱乐部试训。
senses.why: The noun can name a thing tested or a person tested, because both stand in front of a judge.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词既能指被检验的物，也能指被检验的人，因为两者都站在评判者面前。

intro.en: Trial is a noun made in English from the French verb trier, to sift or pick out, and it names whatever has been tested.
intro.cn: trial 是英语用来自法语动词 trier（筛、挑）造出的名词，指被检验过的东西。

items.en: Trier meant to sift grain or to sort things by quality.
items.cn: trier 意为筛谷物或按品质分类。

items.en: Tribulare and tritare lie behind French trier, all about rubbing or sorting.
items.cn: 法语 trier 的背后是 tribulare 与 tritare，都涉及摩擦或分选。

items.en: English formed trial on the French stem, first for the testing of metal and goods.
items.cn: 英语在法语词干上造出 trial，最初指检验金属与货物。

items.en: Law courts adopted the word for the hearing that tests a case.
items.cn: 法院借这个词指检验案情的庭审。

items.en: Everyday speech extended it to anything that tests a person.
items.cn: 日常语言把它扩展到任何考验人的事情。

note.en: The first group shows the try family, the second holds other words for tests and hearings.
note.cn: 第一组是 try 词族，第二组是其他表示测试与审理的词。

entries.definition: To make an attempt or test something.
entries.definitionCN: 尝试；试试

entries.definition: Annoying and hard to bear.
entries.definitionCN: 令人难受的

entries.definition: A test to choose players or workers.
entries.definitionCN: 选拔；试用

entries.definition: A check of quality or ability.
entries.definitionCN: 测试；检验

entries.definition: A session in which a case is examined.
entries.definitionCN: 听证；审理

entries.definition: A controlled attempt to find out something.
entries.definitionCN: 实验

normalIntro.en: Trial is try with a thin -al added: what you get when you try something over and over.
normalIntro.cn: trial 就是 try 加一个轻薄的 -al：反复尝试之后得到的那件事。

normal.en: The y of try becomes i before the suffix: trial.
normal.cn: try 的 y 在词尾前变成 i：trial。

normal.en: Stand trial means you are being tested in court.
normal.cn: stand trial 意为在法庭上受检验。

normal.en: A trial period is time given to see if something works.
normal.cn: trial period 是检验一段时间看是否可行的期限。

normal.en: The plural only adds s: trials.
normal.cn: 复数只加 s：trials。

normal.en: A clinical trial tests a medicine on people.
normal.cn: clinical trial 是在人身上检验药物。

abstract.en: A marker line painted on a test track.
abstract.cn: 试验跑道上画的一条标线。

abstract.en: A small sample of cloth pulled between finger and thumb.
abstract.cn: 指尖搓过的一小块布样。

abstract.en: A long day that keeps asking how much you can carry.
abstract.cn: 漫长的一天，不断问你能承住多少。

examples.en: The drug is being tested in a large clinical trial.
examples.cn: 这种药正在一项大型临床试验中检验。

examples.en: She is standing trial for the theft of two paintings.
examples.cn: 她因盗窃两幅画而受审。

examples.en: The first month is a trial period without any cost.
examples.cn: 第一个月是免付费试用期。

dict_mnemonic.text: trial 里有 try——凡 trial 就是 try 出来的东西。

root: 由法语动词 trier（筛、挑）的词干加 -al 构成，源自中世纪拉丁语 tribulare、tritare，本义与筛选、摩擦有关；同族词有 try、trying、tryout。

sensesIntro.en: First the test of an object, then the test of a case in court, then any hard test of a person.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是检验物件，再是法庭上检验案情，最后是任何对人的艰难考验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marked track and a ticking screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：画着标线的跑道与跳动的屏幕。

branches.en: The product branch: a thing tested before sale.
branches.cn: 产品分支：上市前被检验的东西。

branches.en: The court branch: a case tested by a judge.
branches.cn: 法庭分支：由法官检验的案件。

branches.en: The person branch: a day that tests you.
branches.cn: 人分支：考验你的一天。

branches.en: The testing branch: both asks whether it holds.
branches.cn: 检验分支：两者都在问它是否站得住。

branches.en: The strain branch: weighing a person or a fact.
branches.cn: 承重分支：称量一个人或一项事实。

intro.en: Trial is formed from the French verb stem tri plus the noun suffix -al, a pattern English still uses freely.
intro.cn: trial 由法语动词词干 tri 加名词后缀 -al 构成，这一构词法英语至今仍常用。

latinIntro.en: Latin tritare, to rub or grind, is behind the French stem, and the words below show the same origin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tritare（磨、擦）是法语词干的前身，下面的词显示同一来源。

items.example: The stem carries the act of sorting for quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载按品质分选的行动。

items.example: It turns trying into a trial.
items.exampleCN: 它把尝试变成一次试验。

items.example: The verb names the bare action.
items.exampleCN: 动词命名纯粹的动作。

items.example: The participle became an adjective of strain.
items.exampleCN: 分词变成了表示煎熬的形容词。

items.example: The noun names what was tried.
items.exampleCN: 名词指被试验的那件事。

items.example: Several trials produced the same answer.
items.exampleCN: 几次试验得出同样的答案。

items.meaning: a public test for a place
items.example: Out marks a full attempt to the end.
items.exampleCN: out 标记把事情试到底。

items.example: Re adds another attempt after a failure.
items.exampleCN: re 表示失败后再来一次。

definition_zh: 三角形；三角板；三角关系；三角铁
definition_en: a flat shape with three straight sides and three angles, or an object of that shape
core_image: 三根直棍首尾相接，围出一块有三个角的空地
scene: 黑板上，老师用三条直直的粉笔线围出一块封闭的图形，量角器摆在旁边。Draw a triangle with two equal sides.
sceneCN: 这里 triangle 是「三角形」（第 1 个义项：三条边三个角的平面图形）；句意为画一个两边相等的三角形。三根线首尾相连围出一块地的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 名词换词尾 -ular 构成形容词，义为「三角形的」
由形容词加 -ate 构成动词，义为「用三角测量；使成三角形」
由动词加 -ion 构成名词，义为「三角测量法」

senses.title: A shape with three sides
senses.definition: a flat figure bounded by three straight sides and having three angles
senses.definitionCN: 由三条直边围成、有三个角的平面图形
senses.example: The flag has a red triangle in the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 旗子一角有个红色三角形。
senses.why: The word simply says three angles: tri- is three and gonia is angle in Greek.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面就是「三个角」：tri- 是希腊语的三，gonia 是角。

senses.title: A set square or musical instrument
senses.definition: a flat three-sided tool for drawing or measuring, or a steel rod bent into that shape and struck
senses.definitionCN: 画图测量用的三边形板，或弯成三边形、用来敲击的钢条
senses.example: He played the triangle in the school orchestra.
senses.exampleCN: 他在学校乐队里敲三角铁。
senses.why: An object made in three-sided form takes the name of the form itself.
senses.whyCN: 做成三边形的物件，直接承接了这个形状的名字。

senses.title: A group of three people
senses.definition: a situation in which three people are closely and often awkwardly involved
senses.definitionCN: 三个人紧密牵扯、常常尴尬的局面
senses.example: The novel is built on a love triangle.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说建立在一个三角恋上。
senses.why: Three people pull on one another the way three sides close a figure, so the word pictures the group.
senses.whyCN: 三个人彼此拉扯，正像三条边围住一个图形，于是这个词用来画这种关系。

senses.title: A three-sided area of land or route
senses.definition: a three-sided piece of land, or a route that returns to its start
senses.definitionCN: 呈三角形的地块，或绕回起点的航路
senses.example: The plane flew the triangle between three islands.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机在三座岛之间飞了个三角圈。
senses.why: Any three points can be joined into a closed figure, so a journey among three places borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 任意三点都能连成一个闭合图形，所以三点之间的行程也借用了这个名字。

intro.en: The word is Latin triangulum, a three-cornered figure, from tri-, three, and angulus, a corner.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语 triangulum，即「三角之物」，由 tri-（三）与 angulus（角）构成。

items.en: The root treyes supplies three, and the same root appears in trio and triple.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 treyes 提供「三」，也出现在 trio 与 triple 里。

items.en: Angulus means a corner or an angle, and gives angle, anchor, and anxious through its relatives.
items.cn: 拉丁语 angulus 意为角落、角，其亲族生出 angle、anchor 与 anxious。

items.en: Triangulum means having three corners and is used both of shapes and of land.
items.cn: 拉丁语 triangulum 意为「有三个角」，既指图形也指地块。

items.en: Old French triangle passes the word into English with the plain shape sense.
items.cn: 古法语 triangle 把这个词传入英语，含义就是那个图形。

items.en: Music and later surveying give the word its instrument and its measuring senses.
items.cn: 音乐与后来的测量学给了它乐器和测量用语的义项。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tri- and -angul- pieces, while the near-meaning group gathers other plane figures.
note.cn: 形近组共用 tri- 与 -angul- 两部分，近义组汇集其他平面图形。

entries.definition: having three sides
entries.definitionCN: 三角形的

entries.definition: the space between two meeting lines
entries.definitionCN: 角；角度

entries.definition: three times as much
entries.definitionCN: 三倍的

entries.definition: a three-pronged spear; the prefix is shared, the root differs
entries.definitionCN: 三叉戟；只是前缀相同，词根不同

entries.definition: a figure with four right angles
entries.definitionCN: 长方形

entries.definition: a figure with four equal sides
entries.definitionCN: 正方形

entries.definition: any figure with many straight sides
entries.definitionCN: 多边形

entries.definition: a piece shaped like a narrow triangle
entries.definitionCN: 楔子；三角形块

normalIntro.en: Tri- is three and angle is angle, so the word explains itself.
normalIntro.cn: tri- 是三，angle 是角，这个词自己就把意思说清了。

normal.en: Tri- appears in tripod, triple, and trio, all about three.
normal.cn: tri- 出现在 tripod、triple、trio 里，全都与三有关。

normal.en: Angle is the same word as the one in right angle.
normal.cn: angle 就是 right angle 里的那个 angle。

normal.en: Triangular is the adjective, with -ular replacing the -e.
normal.cn: triangular 是形容词，-ular 替掉了词尾的 -e。

normal.en: A love triangle has three sides that pull against each other.
normal.cn: 三角恋的三条边彼此拉扯。

normal.en: A triangle in an orchestra is a steel rod struck with a stick.
normal.cn: 乐队里的三角铁是一根被小棒敲的钢条。

abstract.en: Picture three matchsticks laid end to end, closing a small yard.
abstract.cn: 想象三根火柴首尾相接，围出一小块院子。

abstract.en: See the angles as three corners the sticks cannot round off.
abstract.cn: 把三个角想成火柴磨不圆的三处尖角。

abstract.en: Set the same yard on three islands and fly around it.
abstract.cn: 把这块院子搁在三座岛上，再绕它飞一圈。

examples.en: The roof is built from two large triangles.
examples.cn: 屋顶由两个大三角形构成。

examples.en: She tapped the triangle once and the hall fell silent.
examples.cn: 她敲了一下三角铁，礼堂立刻安静下来。

examples.en: Their friendship became a triangle when a third classmate joined.
examples.cn: 第三个同学加入后，他们的友谊成了三角。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「揣安钩」——揣着三个安好的钩子，钩成三角形的三个角。

root: 拉丁语 tri-（三）+ angulus（角），名词 triangulum 经古法语进入英语；同族有 angle、triangular、triple

sensesIntro.en: The word names a shape first, then any object or group that takes that shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先给形状命名，再给任何取这一形状的物件或群体命名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three straight sticks closing a small plot of ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：三根直棍围出一小块地。

branches.en: The plain geometric sense, the shape itself.
branches.cn: 朴素几何义：形状本身。

branches.en: The instrument sense, where a made object takes the shape’s name.
branches.cn: 器物义：做成这个形状的东西直接用了名字。

branches.en: The human sense, where three people pull against one another.
branches.cn: 人事义：三个人彼此拉扯。

branches.en: The spatial sense, where land or a route forms the figure.
branches.cn: 空间义：地块或航路形成这个图形。

branches.en: The geometric sense again, where the three corners are what matters.
branches.cn: 再回几何义：关键在三个角。

intro.en: The word joins a Greek-derived number to a Latin word for corner.
intro.cn: 这个词把表示数字的前缀与拉丁语「角」一词连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Angulus is behind angle, triangular, and the whole family of English angle words.
latinIntro.cn: angulus 支撑着 angle、triangular 以及整族英语「角」类词。

items.example: A tripod has three legs.
items.exampleCN: tripod 有三条腿。

items.example: The stem gives angle.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干生出 angle。

items.example: The angle is nearly ninety degrees.
items.exampleCN: 这个角接近九十度。

items.example: He has an angular face.
items.exampleCN: 他的脸棱角分明。

items.example: Triangle gives triangular.
items.exampleCN: triangle 加它成为 triangular。

items.example: Costs tripled in a year.
items.exampleCN: 一年里成本涨了两倍。

items.example: The trio played all evening.
items.exampleCN: 这支三重奏演奏了一整晚。

items.example: Triangular gives triangulate.
items.exampleCN: triangular 加它成为 triangulate。

items.example: Triangulate gives triangulation.
items.exampleCN: triangulate 加它成为 triangulation。

definition_zh: 部落的；按部落组织的；部落社会特有的；（贬义）只认自己群体的
definition_en: relating to a tribe, or organized around tribes rather than around a state
core_image: 同一条纹披肩从左肩绕到右肩，条纹的数目就是辈分的记号，一眼能看出谁该先说话。
scene: 广场上，人们披着相同的条纹披肩，鼓声一响便按辈分站成两排。The dancers wore tribal patterns that showed which family they came from.
sceneCN: 这里 tribal 指「与部落相关的、属于部落的」（第 1 个义项：描述事物归属某一部落）；句意为舞者身上的部落花纹表明他们出自哪个家族。可辨识物件：条纹披肩、鼓、两排舞者、广场、花纹带。

pos.zh: 部落的；部落制的；只认自己群体的

derivatives.zh: 拉丁 tribus「分区」经古法语 tribu → 部落，语义由行政分区扩为亲缘群体
tribal + -ly（副词后缀）→ 以部落方式，语义落在组织形态
tribal + -ism（体系或主张后缀）→ 由形容词转为「宗族忠诚、部落主义」
tribal + -ist（主张者后缀）→ 主张本群体优先的人；带此色彩的
tribalist + -ic（形容词后缀）→ 带有宗派忠诚色彩的
de-（去除）+ tribal + -ize（动词后缀）→ 使脱离部落组织，语义指向制度变迁

senses.title: Belonging to a tribe
senses.definition: of or belonging to a tribe, its members or its territory
senses.definitionCN: 属于某个部落、其成员或其土地的
senses.example: The dancers wore tribal patterns that showed which family they came from.
senses.exampleCN: 舞者身上的部落花纹表明他们出自哪个家族。
senses.why: tribe plus the relational suffix -al produces the plain adjective of belonging.
senses.whyCN: tribe 加关系形容词后缀 -al，就得出表示归属的普通形容词。

senses.title: Organized by tribes, not by a state
senses.titleCN: 按部落而非国家组织的
senses.definition: describing a political order in which authority rests with tribal groups rather than with central institutions
senses.definitionCN: 描述权威属于各部落群体、而非中央机构的政治秩序
senses.example: The region has a tribal order that no capital has ever fully replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区有一套部落秩序，任何首都都未能完全取代。
senses.why: if the basic unit of society is the tribe, then the whole order can be called tribal.
senses.whyCN: 如果社会的基本单位是部落，整个秩序就可以被称为部落制的。

senses.title: Characteristic of tribal society
senses.definition: typical of life in a kinship-based society, such as shared land, elders' councils and inherited roles
senses.definitionCN: 亲缘社会生活的典型特征，如共有土地、长者议事与世袭角色
senses.example: Tribal customs settled the dispute before any court existed.
senses.exampleCN: 在法院出现之前，部落习俗就已经解决了争端。
senses.why: customs that grow from kinship organization are naturally labelled with the adjective of that organization.
senses.whyCN: 从亲缘组织中生长出来的习俗，自然用这种组织的形容词来标记。

senses.title: Fiercely loyal to one's own group
senses.definition: showing strong preference for one's own group and its members over outsiders
senses.definitionCN: 对自群体及其成员表现出强于对外人的偏护
senses.example: Tribal loyalty decided the election long before the speeches began.
senses.exampleCN: 早在演讲开始之前，宗族式的忠诚就已经决定了选举。
senses.why: the loyalty a tribe demands became the defining colour of the adjective, even outside real tribes.
senses.whyCN: 部落所要求的忠诚成了这个形容词的鲜明色彩，即使在真实部落之外也如此。

senses.title: Of traditional patterned design
senses.definition: describing art, cloth or ornament whose patterns come from a particular people's tradition
senses.definitionCN: 描述图案来自某一民族传统的艺术、织物或饰物
senses.example: The museum labels the rugs as tribal work, not factory work.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把这些地毯标为部落手工，而非工厂制品。
senses.why: makers' group identity is written into the pattern, so the adjective moves from people to product.
senses.whyCN: 制作者的群体身份被写进图案，因此这个形容词从人转到了物。

senses.title: Bloc-minded in politics
senses.titleCN: 政治上只认自己一派的（贬义）
senses.definition: acting in narrow factional interest, as if a party were a tribe
senses.definitionCN: 以狭窄派系利益行事，仿佛政党就是部落
senses.example: Commentators called the budget debate tribal rather than ideological.
senses.exampleCN: 评论员说这场预算辩论是宗派之争，而非意识形态之争。
senses.why: when loyalty to a subgroup outranks the common institution, observers reach for the tribal label.
senses.whyCN: 当对小团体的忠诚压过共同制度时，观察者就会取用 tribal 这个标签。

senses.title: Divided into tribes administratively
senses.definition: describing a system that treats the population as a set of tribes for counting or governing
senses.definitionCN: 把人口当作一组部落来统计或治理的制度
senses.example: The tribal districts were drawn to match the old grazing boundaries.
senses.exampleCN: 部落选区是按旧的放牧边界划定的。
senses.why: once officials adopt the tribe as their unit, the resulting map and system are called tribal.
senses.whyCN: 一旦官员采用部落作为单位，由此产生的地图与制度就被称为部落制的。

senses.title: Marked by in-group boundaries
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：以群体归属划界的
senses.definition: any arrangement in which belonging to one group decides trust, access and obligation
senses.definitionCN: 任何由群体归属决定信任、机会与义务的安排
senses.example: The office had a tribal feel: outsiders learned nothing until they married in.
senses.exampleCN: 那间办公室有种部落气息：外人除非娶进去，否则什么也学不到。
senses.why: strip away the ancestors and what remains is the boundary itself, which is the abstract sense.
senses.whyCN: 抽掉祖先，剩下的就是那条边界本身，这就是抽象义。

intro.en: Tribal is tribe plus the Latin-derived suffix -al. The noun came from Latin tribus through Old French; the adjective is an English formation.
intro.cn: tribal 由 tribe 加源自拉丁的后缀 -al 构成。名词经古法语来自拉丁 tribus，形容词则是英语自身的构造。

items.en: Tribus was a division of the Roman people, and its own derivation is uncertain; the hypotheses linking it to tri- 'three' or to tribuere 'to allot' are not established.
items.cn: tribus 是罗马人民的一个分区，其自身来源不确定；把它与 tri-「三」或 tribuere「分配」相联的假说均未证实。

items.en: The noun reached English in the fourteenth century as tribu, first in biblical lists of the twelve tribes.
items.cn: 名词在 14 世纪以 tribu 形式进入英语，最初见于十二支派的圣经清单。

items.en: The suffix -alis had long supplied English adjectives of relation, so tribe plus -al needed no Latin model.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 早已为英语提供关系形容词，因此 tribe 加 -al 无须拉丁范本。

items.en: Tribal appears in English writing of the seventeenth century, first describing peoples and their customs.
items.cn: tribal 见于 17 世纪的英语写作，最初描述各个民族及其习俗。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective extended to design, politics and institutional loyalty, where no actual tribe exists.
items.cn: 到 20 世纪，这个形容词扩展到设计、政治与机构忠诚，那里并没有真实的部落。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest use of tribal is only approximately dated, and the origin of tribus remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：tribal 的最早用法只有约数，tribus 的来源仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same word family that are often swapped by mistake; group two holds adjectives for social orders that are not tribal.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族中常被误换的形式；第二组是描述非部落社会秩序的形容词。

entries.definition: The group itself; tribal is only its adjective and cannot replace it in a sentence like 'the tribe met'.
entries.definitionCN: 群体本身；tribal 只是它的形容词，不能代替「部落开会」这类句子里的名词。

entries.definition: Loyalty to one's group; it is a noun of attitude, while tribal describes what has that attitude or structure.
entries.definitionCN: 对本群体的忠诚；它是态度名词，而 tribal 描述带有这种态度或结构的事物。

entries.definition: In a tribal manner; it modifies verbs, as in land held tribally.
entries.definitionCN: 以部落方式；修饰动词，如土地由部落共有。

entries.definition: A Roman office or a raised platform; it shares letters with tribe but names no people.
entries.definitionCN: 罗马官职或讲台；与 tribe 共享字母，却不指任何族群。

entries.definition: Relating to a people's culture or descent; it is the neutral choice where tribal would sound loaded.
entries.definitionCN: 关于一个民族的文化或血统；在 tribal 显得带偏见处，它是中性选择。

entries.definition: Keeping tightly to one's family or circle and cold to outsiders; it stresses exclusion rather than organization.
entries.definitionCN: 紧抱自家或自己圈子、对外人冷淡；强调排外而非组织形态。

entries.definition: Tied to a place; a tribal order is tied to descent, which local does not say.
entries.definitionCN: 与地点相连；部落秩序与血统相连，而 local 不含此意。

entries.definition: Held or done in common; it describes ownership, while tribal describes the social unit that owns.
entries.definitionCN: 共同持有或共同进行；它描述所有权，tribal 描述持有的社会单位。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real noun-plus-suffix build, real relatives and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的名词加后缀构造、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: tribe + -al: the adjective of belonging, nothing more elaborate.
normal.cn: tribe + -al：表示归属的形容词，没有更复杂的构造。

normal.en: The family runs tribe, tribal, tribally, tribalism, tribalist, tribalistic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tribe、tribal、tribally、tribalism、tribalist、tribalistic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: tribal elders, tribal land, tribal loyalty.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：部落长者、部落土地、宗族式忠诚。

normal.en: The stress stays on the first syllable: TRIB-al, like TRIBE.
normal.cn: 重音留在第一音节：TRIB-al，与 TRIBE 一致。

normal.en: Detribalize reverses the adjective with de- and -ize.
normal.cn: detribalize 用 de- 与 -ize 把这一形容词反向动词化。

abstract.en: Picture a striped shawl that tells every stranger your rank before you speak.
abstract.cn: 想象一条条纹披肩，在你开口之前就向每个陌生人说明了你的辈分。

abstract.en: Picture a map coloured by group rather than by river.
abstract.cn: 想象一张按群体、而不是按河流上色的地图。

abstract.en: Picture an office where the org chart is drawn like a family tree.
abstract.cn: 想象一间办公室，组织图被画成了家谱。

examples.en: Tribal elders still settle most boundary quarrels without a lawyer.
examples.cn: 部落长者仍然不用律师就解决大多数边界纠纷。

examples.en: The label tribal is now avoided where ethnic group would be clearer.
examples.cn: 在 ethnic group 更清楚的地方，如今避免使用 tribal 这个标签。

examples.en: The debate turned tribal once each side began defending its own members only.
examples.cn: 一旦双方都只护自己人，辩论就变成了宗派之争。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「tribe（部落）+ al（的）」——属于部落的 → 部落的、只认自己人的

root: 英语 tribe（拉丁 tribus「分区」经古法语 tribu）+ 拉丁系形容词后缀 -al；tribus 自身来源不确定，相关假说均未证实。英语 tribal。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one relation: belonging to a tribe. The relation is then read as a political order, a set of customs, a loyalty, a design style, a factional habit, an administrative map and finally any boundary of belonging.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种关系展开：归属于某个部落。这种关系再依次被读作政治秩序、习俗体系、忠诚、图案风格、派系习气、行政划分，最后读作任何归属边界。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a striped shawl that announces rank and family before a word is spoken.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条条纹披肩，在人开口之前就说明辈分与家族。

branches.en: BELONG AND ADMINISTER: the same adjective marks a people's own things and the map an office draws of them.
branches.cn: 归属与行政：同一个形容词既标记一个民族自己的东西，也标记机关画出的地图。

branches.en: ORDER AND CUSTOM: rule by tribes and the habits that grow under it are two sides of one arrangement.
branches.cn: 秩序与习俗：部落掌权与在其下生长的习惯，是同一安排的两面。

branches.en: LOYALTY AND FACTION: warm loyalty inside becomes cold factionalism outside.
branches.cn: 忠诚与派系：对内的热忠诚，对外就成了冷派系。

branches.en: PATTERN STYLE: the group's identity passes into cloth and ornament.
branches.cn: 图案风格：群体身份进入织物与饰物。

branches.en: BOUNDARY: remove the tribe and only the line between insiders and outsiders remains.
branches.cn: 边界：去掉部落，只剩圈内人与圈外人之间那条线。

intro.en: Tribal is a noun with one relational suffix; the wider family adds -ism, -ist and the reversive de-.
intro.cn: tribal 是一个名词加一个关系后缀；更大的词族再加 -ism、-ist 与反向前缀 de-。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribus supplies the noun and -alis the suffix pattern; tribuere stands behind tribute but not certainly behind tribus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tribus 提供名词，-alis 提供后缀模式；tribuere 是 tribute 的来源，但不一定是 tribus 的来源。

items.example: The Latin noun already named a slice of a people.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词本义就指人群中的一块。

items.example: The suffix passed into English as -al.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀以 -al 形式进入英语。

items.structure: tribus (Latin) → Old French tribu → English tribe
items.example: The noun is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是形容词的基础。

items.example: Tribe plus -al yields tribal.
items.exampleCN: tribe 加 -al 得出 tribal。

items.example: Tribal plus -ly yields tribally.

items.example: Tribal plus -ism yields tribalism.
items.exampleCN: tribal 加 -ism 得出 tribalism。

items.example: Tribal plus -ist yields tribalist.
items.exampleCN: tribal 加 -ist 得出 tribalist。

items.example: Tribalist plus -ic yields tribalistic.
items.exampleCN: tribalist 加 -ic 得出 tribalistic。

items.example: De- plus tribal plus -ize yields detribalize.
items.exampleCN: de- 加 tribal 再加 -ize 得出 detribalize。

items.exampleCN: 宗族忠诚使这个形容词所描述的边界更加坚硬。

definition_zh: 部落主义；宗族忠诚；以部落为基础的社会制度；排外的小团体意识
definition_en: strong loyalty to one's own tribe or group over the wider society, and social organization built on tribes
core_image: 两条村路并排通向同一座桥，上桥后各自只走一边，谁也不肯让谁先过。
scene: 两条村路并排通向同一座桥，上桥后各自靠一边走，谁也不肯让谁先过。Tribalism kept the two valleys apart long after the road joined them.
sceneCN: 这里 tribalism 指「对本部落或本群体的忠诚高于对更大社会的忠诚」（第 1 个义项：以本群体为先的忠诚与做法）；句意为道路把两处山谷连起来很久之后，宗族式的忠诚仍让它们彼此分隔。可辨识物件：两条村路、石桥、两侧行人、界石、山谷。

pos.zh: 部落主义；宗族忠诚；部落制度

derivatives.zh: tribe + -al（关系形容词后缀）→ 由「部落」转为「部落的」
tribal + -ist（主张者后缀）→ 以本群体为先的人，语义由性质转为人
tribalist + -ic（形容词后缀）→ 带有宗派忠诚色彩的
de-（去除）+ tribal + -ize（动词后缀）→ 使脱离部落组织，语义指向制度变迁
detribalize + -ation（过程名词后缀）→ 脱离部落组织的过程

senses.title: Loyalty to one's group before society
senses.titleCN: 对本群体的忠诚高于更大社会
senses.definition: the habit of putting one's own tribe or group first, even when the wider society suffers
senses.definitionCN: 把本部落或本群体放在首位、即使更大社会受损也如此的习惯
senses.example: Tribalism kept the two valleys apart long after the road joined them.
senses.exampleCN: 道路把两处山谷连起来很久之后，宗族式的忠诚仍让它们彼此分隔。
senses.why: the suffix -ism turns tribal into the name of an attitude, and that attitude is loyalty to the tribe.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ism 把 tribal 变成一种态度的名称，而这种态度就是对本部落的忠诚。

senses.title: Organization of the state by tribes
senses.titleCN: 以部落为基础的国家组织方式
senses.definition: a political system in which tribal units, not central offices, hold the real power
senses.definitionCN: 由部落单位而非中央机关掌握实权的政治制度
senses.example: Tribalism in the province meant every ministry job belonged to a valley.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个省，部落主义意味着每个部门的职位都归某条山谷。
senses.why: if the tribe is the unit that governs, the system itself takes the name of that unit.
senses.whyCN: 如果部落是治理单位，这套制度就以这个单位命名。

senses.title: Tribal social organization as studied
senses.titleCN: 人类学研究的部落型社会组织
senses.definition: the form of social organization in which kinship groups, not classes or offices, set the order
senses.definitionCN: 由亲缘群体而非阶级或职位决定秩序的社会组织形式
senses.example: The early survey described tribalism as a stage rather than a stain.
senses.exampleCN: 早期调查报告把部落组织描述为一个阶段，而不是污点。
senses.why: researchers first used the word neutrally for a type of organization, before it acquired its critical tone.
senses.whyCN: 研究者最初中性使用这个词，指一种组织类型，后来它才带上批评口吻。

senses.title: Sectarian hostility toward outsiders
senses.titleCN: 贬义：对外人的宗派敌意
senses.definition: a narrow and hostile preference for one's own group, with suspicion of everyone outside it
senses.definitionCN: 对本群体狭隘而敌意的偏护，对圈外一切人抱有怀疑
senses.example: The report blamed tribalism for the collapse of the shared council.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把共同议会的瓦解归咎于宗派主义。
senses.why: loyalty inside a group looks like hostility from outside, and modern usage usually takes that outside view.
senses.whyCN: 群体内的忠诚从外面看就是敌意，现代用法通常采取这个外部视角。

senses.title: Pride in tribal identity
senses.titleCN: 对部落身份与文化的自豪
senses.definition: a positive attachment to one's people's language, customs and history
senses.definitionCN: 对本民族语言、习俗与历史的正面依恋
senses.example: The festival celebrates tribalism as heritage, not as division.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆把部落认同当作遗产来庆祝，而不是当作分裂。
senses.why: the same loyalty can be praised as heritage when the speaker stands inside the group.
senses.whyCN: 当说话人站在群体内部时，同一种忠诚就会被赞为遗产。

senses.title: Factionalism inside an institution
senses.definition: the tendency of departments or teams to defend their own members against the whole organization
senses.definitionCN: 部门或团队护自己成员、对抗整个机构的倾向
senses.example: Tribalism between departments delayed the merger by a year.
senses.exampleCN: 部门之间的派系主义让合并推迟了一年。
senses.why: a company can reproduce the tribe's structure, so the critical sense transfers to offices.
senses.whyCN: 公司可以复制部落的结构，因此这个批评义项也转移到办公室。

senses.title: Any in-group bias
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何内群体偏私
senses.definition: the general tendency to favour insiders and distrust outsiders, whatever the group may be
senses.definitionCN: 偏护圈内人、怀疑圈外人的普遍倾向，不论群体是什么
senses.example: Fans show tribalism even when the teams are made of strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 即使球队由陌生人组成，球迷仍表现出内群体偏私。
senses.why: the abstract sense drops tribe, kin and land and keeps only the insider boundary.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义丢掉部落、亲缘与土地，只保留圈内边界。

senses.title: Revival of tribal tradition
senses.definition: a movement to restore tribal language, law or ceremony after a period of suppression
senses.definitionCN: 在压制期之后恢复部落语言、法律或仪式的运动
senses.example: The school was founded as tribalism in the best sense, a recovery of lost songs.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校是作为最好意义上的部落传统复兴而创办的，找回失传的歌。
senses.why: when a tradition returns, the word can name the movement rather than the bias.
senses.whyCN: 当传统回归时，这个词可以指那场运动，而不是指偏见。

intro.en: Tribalism is tribal plus -ism. The noun tribe came from Latin tribus through Old French, and the derivative is an English formation of the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: tribalism 由 tribal 加 -ism 构成。名词 tribe 经古法语来自拉丁 tribus，这一派生词是 19 世纪的英语构造。

items.en: Tribus named a division of the Roman people; its own origin is uncertain, and the hypotheses connecting it to tri- 'three' or to tribuere 'to allot' are not established.
items.cn: tribus 指罗马人民的一个分区，其自身来源不确定；把它与 tri-「三」或 tribuere「分配」相联的假说均未证实。

items.en: English tribe arrived in the fourteenth century through Old French tribu, first in biblical lists of the twelve tribes.
items.cn: 英语 tribe 在 14 世纪经古法语 tribu 传入，最初见于十二支派的圣经清单。

items.en: Tribal appears in the seventeenth century; the adjective made a noun of attitude easy to form.
items.cn: tribal 出现在 17 世纪；这个形容词使表示态度的名词很容易构造。

items.en: The suffix -ismus names systems and doctrines, so tribal plus -ism produced a word for loyalty to tribes as a principle.
items.cn: 后缀 -ismus 标记体系与主张，因此 tribal 加 -ism 造出了把部落忠诚当作原则的词。

items.en: Colonial administrators and early anthropologists used tribalism for social organization, often ranking it against their own institutions.
items.cn: 殖民官员与早期人类学家用 tribalism 指社会组织形式，往往把它与自身制度排成高低。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest use of tribalism is only approximately dated, and the origin of tribus remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：tribalism 的最早用法只有约数，tribus 的来源仍无定论。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same family that are routinely confused with the attitude noun; group two holds words for group partiality in other frames.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族中常与这一态度名词混淆的形式；第二组是其他框架下表示群体偏私的词。

entries.definition: Describing what belongs to a tribe; tribalism is the attitude or system itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述属于部落的事物；tribalism 是态度或制度本身。

entries.definition: The people themselves; tribalism can outlast any actual tribe.
entries.definitionCN: 指人群本身；tribalism 可以比任何真实部落活得更久。

entries.definition: A person who puts the group first; the -ist suffix marks the supporter, not the doctrine.
entries.definitionCN: 把本群体放在首位的人；-ist 标记支持者，而不是主张。

entries.definition: From Latin tribulare 'to thresh, afflict', built on tribulum 'threshing sledge'; it shares a prefix of sound only.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 tribulare「打谷、使受苦」，由 tribulum「打谷板」构成，仅读音开头相近。

entries.definition: The splitting of an organization into rival cliques; it is the office version of tribalism.
entries.definitionCN: 组织分裂为对立小集团；它是部落主义在办公室里的版本。

entries.definition: Hostility between religious or political sects; it adds doctrine, which tribalism need not have.
entries.definitionCN: 宗教或政治派别之间的敌意；它含有教义成分，而部落主义不必有。

entries.definition: Loyalty to a nation-state; it is loyalty upward in scale, while tribalism is loyalty to a smaller unit.
entries.definitionCN: 对民族国家的忠诚；是规模更大的忠诚，而部落主义是对更小单位的忠诚。

entries.definition: Favouring relatives in appointments; it is one practical form that tribalism can take.
entries.definitionCN: 任用亲属；它是部落主义可能采取的一种实际形式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real adjective-plus-suffix build, real relatives and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的形容词加后缀构造、真实同族词与真实搭配。

normal.en: tribal + -ism: loyalty to the tribe raised to a principle.
normal.cn: tribal + -ism：把对部落的忠诚提升为一条原则。

normal.en: The family runs tribe, tribal, tribalism, tribalist, tribalistic, detribalize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tribe、tribal、tribalism、tribalist、tribalistic、detribalize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the criticism: political tribalism, ethnic tribalism, overcome tribalism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出批评语境：政治派系主义、族群宗派主义、克服宗派观念。

normal.en: Compare factionalism: the same shape inside a company instead of a valley.
normal.cn: 对照 factionalism：同样的形状，发生在公司里而不是山谷里。

normal.en: Detribalize is the verb that names the opposite movement.
normal.cn: detribalize 是命名相反运动的动词。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge wide enough for everyone, used one half at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一座宽得能容下所有人的桥，却每次只用一半。

abstract.en: Picture a hiring committee that reads surnames before files.
abstract.cn: 想象一个招聘委员会，先看姓氏再看材料。

abstract.en: Picture a stadium where the same city cheers two different halves.
abstract.cn: 想象一座体育场，同一座城市为两个不同的半场欢呼。

examples.en: Economists warn that tribalism raises the cost of every public project.
examples.cn: 经济学家警告说，宗派主义会抬高每一项公共工程的成本。

examples.en: The novel treats tribalism as both shelter and cage.
examples.cn: 这部小说把部落认同既写成庇护，也写成牢笼。

examples.en: Reformers hoped railways would weaken tribalism; instead the lines carried it farther.
examples.cn: 改革者原指望铁路削弱宗族观念，结果铁路把它带得更远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「tribal（部落的）+ ism（主义）」——把本部落放在所有人前面 → 部落主义、宗派忠诚

root: 英语 tribal（tribe + -al，源自拉丁 tribus「分区」）+ -ism（体系或主张后缀）；tribus 自身来源不确定，相关假说均未证实。英语 tribalism。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one preference: my group before the wider whole. The preference is read as a system, a research category, hostility, pride, office factionalism, a general bias and finally a movement to restore what was lost.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种偏好展开：本群体先于更大的整体。这种偏好再依次被读作制度、研究类别、敌意、自豪、职场派系、普遍偏私，最后读作恢复失落的运动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bridge used one half at a time by people who could share it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座本可共享的桥，被两边的人分半使用。

branches.en: FIRST AND HOSTILE: the same preference looks like warmth inside and enmity outside.
branches.cn: 优先与敌意：同一种偏护，对内是温暖，对外是敌意。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND STUDY: rule by tribes and the category used to describe it share one name.
branches.cn: 制度与研究：部落掌权与描述它的类别共用同一个名称。

branches.en: PRIDE AND REVIVAL: attachment to one's own culture can be celebrated or rebuilt.
branches.cn: 自豪与复兴：对本文化的依恋，可以被庆祝，也可以被重建。

branches.en: OFFICE FACTION: a company reproduces the valley's boundary inside one building.
branches.cn: 职场派系：公司在一栋楼里复制了山谷的边界。

branches.en: GENERAL BIAS: remove tribe and kin, and only the insider line is left.
branches.cn: 普遍偏私：去掉部落与亲缘，只剩圈内那条线。

intro.en: Tribalism is an English adjective plus a Greek-derived suffix; the wider family adds -ist, -istic and the reversive de-.
intro.cn: tribalism 是英语形容词加源自希腊的后缀；更大的词族再加 -ist、-istic 与反向前缀 de-。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribus supplies the base noun, while the suffix -ismus came to English through Latin from Greek -ismos.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tribus 提供基础名词，而后缀 -ismus 经拉丁语从希腊语 -ismos 进入英语。

items.meaning: a division of the Roman people
items.example: The base noun named an administrative slice of a people.
items.exampleCN: 基础名词指人群中的一个行政切片。

items.structure: tribus (Latin) → Old French tribu → English tribe
items.example: Tribe is the noun behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: tribe 是这一形容词背后的名词。

items.example: Tribe plus -al yields tribal.
items.exampleCN: tribe 加 -al 得出 tribal。

items.example: Tribal plus -ism yields tribalism.
items.exampleCN: tribal 加 -ism 得出 tribalism。

items.example: Tribal plus -ist yields tribalist.
items.exampleCN: tribal 加 -ist 得出 tribalist。

items.example: Tribalist plus -istic yields tribalistic.
items.exampleCN: tribalist 加 -istic 得出 tribalistic。

items.example: De- plus tribal plus -ize yields detribalize.
items.exampleCN: de- 加 tribal 再加 -ize 得出 detribalize。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a verb of change.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成表示变化的动词。

items.example: Detribalize plus -ation yields detribalization.
items.exampleCN: detribalize 加 -ation 得出 detribalization。

items.meaning: one who puts the group first
items.meaningCN: 把本群体放在首位的人
items.example: The tribalist trusted no outside referee.
items.exampleCN: 这位宗派拥护者不信任任何外部裁判。

latinEntries.meaning: a division of the Roman people

definition_zh: 部落；民族的支系；（非正式）一大家子；有共同趣味的小圈子
definition_en: a group of people linked by kinship, language and territory, and by extension any close-knit circle
core_image: 一圈人围着同一堆火，火光照出同一张亲缘网，网外的人站在暗处。
scene: 清晨的河边，几十个人围着火堆坐成一圈，长者先开口，年轻人依次应答。Herders of the tribe move camp whenever the water sinks.
sceneCN: 这里 tribe 指「由血缘、语言与地域联结起来的群体」（第 1 个义项：以亲缘关系为核心的人群单位）；句意为这个部落的牧人在水位下降时就迁营。可辨识物件：火堆、围坐的人、河岸、帐篷、水罐。

pos.zh: 部落；支系；（非正式）家族、圈子

derivatives.zh: tribe + -al（关系形容词后缀）→ 由「部落」转为「部落的」
tribal + -ly（副词后缀）→ 以部落的方式，语义落在组织形态
tribal + -ism（体系或主张后缀）→ 由形容词转为「部落主义、宗族忠诚」
tribal + -ist（从事者或主张者后缀）→ 信奉本群体优先的人
tribe + -let（指小后缀）→ 规模很小的部落单位，语义缩小

senses.title: A group bound by kinship and place
senses.titleCN: 以血缘、语言与地域联结的群体
senses.definition: a community whose members trace common descent, speak one language and hold one stretch of country
senses.definitionCN: 成员共有祖先、使用同一种语言、占有同一片土地的共同体
senses.example: Herders of the tribe move camp whenever the water sinks.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部落的牧人在水位下降时就迁营。
senses.why: the Roman tribus named a division of the people, and the English word kept that sense of a bounded slice of a larger population.
senses.whyCN: 罗马的 tribus 指人民中的一个分支，英语继承了这个「较大人群中的一块」的意思。

senses.title: A label for pre-state societies
senses.titleCN: 人类学中以前国家社会为对象的泛称
senses.definition: a general term used by researchers for societies organized by kinship rather than by a state, now often treated with caution
senses.definitionCN: 研究者用来指按亲缘而非国家组织的社会，如今常被谨慎使用
senses.example: The textbook warns that tribe is a loose label, not a legal category.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书提醒说，tribe 是宽松的标签，不是法律类别。
senses.why: nineteenth-century writers needed one word for peoples without states, so they widened the older word far beyond its Roman meaning.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪的作者需要用一个词概括没有国家的人群，于是把旧词的含义远远扩展到罗马义之外。

senses.title: A branch of a whole people
senses.definition: one of the named divisions of a people, as in the twelve tribes of Israel
senses.definitionCN: 一个民族中被命名的分支之一，如以色列十二支派
senses.example: Each tribe supplied one gate of the city in the old account.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧记载中，每个支派负责城门中的一座。
senses.why: the biblical use fixed the word as a division within one people, which is the closest English sense to Latin tribus.
senses.whyCN: 《圣经》用法把这个词固定为同一民族内部的分支，这是英语中最接近拉丁 tribus 的义项。

senses.title: A large family, informally
senses.definition: a person's extended family or a crowd of relatives, said with a smile rather than as a technical term
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的大家族或一群亲戚，带玩笑口吻，而非术语
senses.example: Half the tribe turned up for the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 一大家子有一半人出现在婚礼上。
senses.why: if a tribe is a kinship group, any big family can be called one in jest.
senses.whyCN: 既然部落就是亲缘群体，任何大家庭都可以被戏称为一个部落。

senses.title: A circle with shared taste
senses.definition: a close group of people who share an interest, style or occupation and keep outsiders at a distance
senses.definitionCN: 兴趣、风格或职业相同、并对外人保持距离的紧密群体
senses.example: The tribe of coffee obsessives knows every roaster in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡痴迷者的圈子认识城里每一家烘焙商。
senses.why: the kinship image survives in the group's loyalty and its clear edge, even when no ancestor is shared.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有共同祖先，群体内部的忠诚与清晰的边界仍保留了亲缘意象。

senses.title: A bloc inside a larger body
senses.definition: a faction within a party or institution that acts for its own members before the whole
senses.definitionCN: 政党或机构内部、先顾自己成员再顾整体的派系
senses.example: The party split into three tribes before the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 投票前，这个党分裂成了三派。
senses.why: a tribe's loyalty to its own people is exactly what a faction shows, so the word moves easily into politics.
senses.whyCN: 部落对自家人优先的忠诚，正是派系所表现出的东西，因此这个词很容易进入政治语境。
