senses.title: An administrative unit
senses.titleCN: 殖民与行政语境中的管理单位
senses.definition: a unit used by officials to count, tax or govern a population, often drawn with little regard for real ties
senses.definitionCN: 官员用来统计、征税或治理人群的单位，划分时常不顾真实关系
senses.example: The old register lists the village as one tribe of four hundred souls.
senses.exampleCN: 旧登记册把这个村子列为一个四百人的部落单位。
senses.why: governments needed countable units, and they borrowed the word for a people and turned it into a box on a form.
senses.whyCN: 政府需要可计数的单位，于是借来指人群的词，把它变成表格上的一格。

senses.title: Any group one is born into
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何与生俱来的归属群体
senses.definition: any group whose membership comes by birth and which expects loyalty before choice
senses.definitionCN: 成员身份由出生决定、并要求忠诚先于选择的任何群体
senses.example: For him the firm was a tribe, entered at birth and never left.
senses.exampleCN: 对他来说，那家公司就是一个部落，生来就在其中，从未离开。
senses.why: the abstract sense keeps the structure of birth plus loyalty and drops the land and the ancestors.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了「出生加忠诚」的结构，丢掉了土地与祖先。

intro.en: Tribe comes from Latin tribus, the name of a division of the Roman people, through Old French tribu. The origin of tribus itself is uncertain.
intro.cn: tribe 经古法语 tribu 来自拉丁 tribus，后者是罗马人民中一个分支的名称。tribus 本身的来源不确定。

items.en: Tribus named one of the divisions into which Roman citizens were enrolled. Its own origin is uncertain: a link with tri- 'three' and a link with tribuere 'to allot' are both offered as hypotheses, and neither is established.
items.cn: tribus 指罗马公民被编入的各个分支之一。它自身的来源不确定：与 tri-「三」的联系、与 tribuere「分配」的联系都只是假说，两者均未得到证实。

items.en: In the Republic the tribus were voting divisions, not ethnic groups, so the Latin word already meant an administrative slice of a people.
items.cn: 在共和国时期，tribus 是投票分区，而非族群，因此这个拉丁词本义就是人民中的一个行政切片。

items.en: Old French tribu brought the word into English in the fourteenth century, first in biblical passages about the twelve tribes.
items.cn: 古法语 tribu 在 14 世纪把该词带入英语，最初见于关于十二支派的圣经段落。

items.en: From the eighteenth century travellers applied the word to peoples across Asia, Africa and the Americas, often with little knowledge of their institutions.
items.cn: 从 18 世纪起，旅行者把这个词用于亚洲、非洲与美洲各地的族群，往往对其制度所知甚少。

items.en: Twentieth-century anthropology treated tribe as a loose category and often replaced it with more precise terms such as band or lineage.
items.cn: 20 世纪的人类学把 tribe 视为宽松类别，常用 band（小游群）或 lineage（世系群）等更精确的词替代。

items.en: Source uncertain (origin and first date): the derivation of tribus is unsettled, and the earliest English citation is only approximately dated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词源与首见年代）：tribus 的派生关系无定论，最早的英语书证只有约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that resemble tribe in sound or derivation but differ in meaning; group two holds terms for human groups that differ in scale and in how membership is defined.
note.cn: 第一组是读音或词源上与 tribe 相近、但意义不同的词；第二组是人群单位，差别在规模与成员资格的界定方式。

entries.definition: The adjective describing anything of a tribe; it cannot stand for the group itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述与部落有关之事的形容词，不能代替群体本身。

entries.definition: Loyalty to one's own group above the wider society; it names an attitude or system, not a people.
entries.definitionCN: 对本群体优先于大社会的忠诚；它指态度或制度，而非一个族群。

entries.definition: From Latin tributum, from tribuere 'to allot, pay'; whether tribus itself comes from tribuere is disputed, so the two words are not simply one root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 tributum，出自动词 tribuere「分配、支付」；tribus 是否也出自 tribuere 尚有争议，因此两者并非简单的同一词根。

entries.definition: From tribunus, an officer tied to the tribus; in English it means a Roman magistrate or a raised platform, not a people.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 tribunus，是与 tribus 相关的官员；英语中指罗马长官或讲台，不指族群。

entries.definition: A group of families claiming one ancestor; a tribe may contain several clans, so clan is the smaller unit.
entries.definitionCN: 自称出自同一祖先的若干家庭；一个部落可含数个氏族，因此氏族是更小的单位。

entries.definition: A group defined by shared culture, language or descent; it is the neutral term preferred in modern writing.
entries.definitionCN: 以共同文化、语言或血统界定的群体，是现代写作偏好的中性说法。

entries.definition: A people organized as a state or claiming one; it is larger and more political than a tribe.
entries.definitionCN: 组织为国家或主张建国的民族，比部落更大、更具政治性。

entries.definition: A small group of a few families who move and hunt together; anthropologists treat it as smaller than a tribe.
entries.definitionCN: 由几户人家组成、共同迁移与狩猎的小群体；人类学视其为比部落更小的单位。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin division, real relatives and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁分区、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin tribus was a division of the Roman people, so tribe began as a slice of a larger whole.
normal.cn: 拉丁 tribus 是罗马人民的一个分区，因此 tribe 最初指较大整体中的一块。

normal.en: The family runs tribe, tribal, tribally, tribalism, tribalist and tribelet.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 tribe、tribal、tribally、tribalism、tribalist、tribelet。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale: a nomadic tribe, an indigenous tribe, tribe and nation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规模：游牧部落、原住民部落、部落与国家。

normal.en: The biblical twelve tribes fixed the sense of a branch within one people.
normal.cn: 圣经中的十二支派固定了「同一民族内分支」这一义项。

normal.en: Anthropology now prefers band, lineage or ethnic group for precise work.
normal.cn: 人类学如今在精确研究中更偏好 band、lineage 或 ethnic group。

abstract.en: Picture one fire with a fixed ring of faces around it and a dark ring of backs beyond.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆火，前面是一圈固定的面孔，后面是一圈背对火光的黑影。

abstract.en: Picture a family reunion where the seating chart is the family tree.
abstract.cn: 想象一次家庭聚会，座位表就是那棵家谱树。

abstract.en: Picture a club with no membership card, only a shared accent.
abstract.cn: 想象一个没有会员卡的俱乐部，凭的只是同一种口音。

examples.en: The tribe's grazing rights were written down only in the elders' memory.
examples.cn: 这个部落的放牧权只记在长者们的记忆里。

examples.en: Officials counted the tribe as one unit and ignored its internal divisions.
examples.cn: 官员把这个部落当作一个单位来统计，忽略了它内部的分支。

examples.en: At the conference the two tribes of researchers sat at opposite tables.
examples.cn: 会上，两个研究圈子坐在相对的桌旁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「try（试着）+ be（成为）」——试着成为同一群人 → 部落、支系

root: 拉丁 tribus「罗马人民的一个分区」，经古法语 tribu 入英语；tribus 自身来源不确定，与 tri-「三」及 tribuere「分配」的联系均为假说。英语 tribe。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: a bounded slice of a people. The slice is read as a kinship community, a research label, a biblical branch, a family, a taste circle, a political bloc, an office unit and finally any group entered by birth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形状展开：人群中被划出的一块。这块再依次被读作亲缘共同体、研究标签、圣经支派、大家庭、趣味圈子、政治派系、行政单位，最后读作任何凭出生进入的群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one fire with a fixed ring of faces and a dark ring beyond it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一堆火，一圈固定面孔，圈外是一片暗影。

branches.en: KIN AND FAMILY: from a people's division down to one's relatives, the bond is always descent.
branches.cn: 亲缘与家庭：从民族的分支到自己的亲戚，纽带始终是血统。

branches.en: LABEL AND SCRIPTURE: the same word serves a researcher's category and a sacred list of branches.
branches.cn: 标签与经文：同一个词既作研究类别，也作神圣的支派清单。

branches.en: TASTE CIRCLE: shared style does the work of shared ancestry.
branches.cn: 趣味圈子：共同风格替代了共同祖先的作用。

branches.en: BLOC AND BOX: inside a party it is a faction; on a form it is a countable unit.
branches.cn: 派系与表格：在政党内部它是派系，在表格上是可计数的单位。

branches.en: BIRTH-GROUP: keep only birth and loyalty, and any institution can become a tribe.
branches.cn: 出生群体：只留出生与忠诚，任何机构都能变成一个部落。

intro.en: Tribe is a Latin noun with no prefix; English adds -al, -ism and -let to build the family.
intro.cn: tribe 是一个不含前缀的拉丁名词；英语加 -al、-ism 与 -let 构成词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribus gives the noun; the related verb tribuere 'to allot' stands behind tribute and tribune, but the exact link to tribus is disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tribus 给出名词；相关动词 tribuere「分配」是 tribute 与 tribune 的来源，但它与 tribus 的确切联系有争议。

items.meaning: a division of the Roman people
items.example: The noun already meant an administrative slice.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词本义就是行政上的一块。

items.structure: tribuere, tribui, tributum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb stands behind tribute, not directly behind tribe.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是 tribute 的来源，而不是 tribe 的直接来源。

items.example: Tribe plus -al yields tribal.
items.exampleCN: tribe 加 -al 得出 tribal。

items.example: Tribal plus -ly yields tribally.
items.exampleCN: tribal 加 -ly 得出 tribally。

items.example: Tribal plus -ism yields tribalism.
items.exampleCN: tribal 加 -ism 得出 tribalism。

items.example: Tribal plus -ist yields tribalist.
items.exampleCN: tribal 加 -ist 得出 tribalist。

items.example: Tribe plus -let yields tribelet, a small tribal unit.
items.exampleCN: tribe 加 -let 得出 tribelet，即小型部落单位。

items.example: Tribal land is held by the group, not the individual.
items.exampleCN: 部落土地由群体而非个人持有。

items.example: Tribalism can outlast the tribe itself.
items.exampleCN: 宗族忠诚可以比部落本身活得更久。

latinEntries.meaning: a division of the Roman people

definition_zh: 贡品；贡赋；敬意；悼词；颂词；（矿业）矿产分成
definition_en: a payment by one ruler or state to another as a sign of submission, or an expression of respect and admiration
core_image: 石阶下的一只木箱被打开，里面是金片与香料，抬箱的人低着头
scene: 王座前的石阶上，远方来使跪献一箱黄金与香料，作为臣服的表示。The province sent tribute every spring to the capital.
sceneCN: 这里 tribute 指「属地向宗主定期缴纳的贡赋」（第 1 个义项：作为臣服的财物缴纳）；句意为该省每年春天向都城进贡。

pos.zh: 贡品；贡赋；敬意；颂词（可数或不可数）

derivatives.zh: tribute + -ary（属于…的）→ 支流；进贡的（语义偏移：向大河「进贡」的小河）
con-（共同）+ tribuere（分配）→ 贡献（同根，语义偏移：共同给出）
contribute + -ion（动作）→ 贡献；捐款
contribute + -or（施动者）→ 贡献者；投稿人
dis-（分开）+ tribuere → 分发（同根，语义偏移：分开给出）
ad-（向）+ tribuere → 归因于；属性（同根，语义偏移：把某物归到某人名下）

senses.title: Payment by a subject state to a ruler
senses.titleCN: 属国向宗主缴纳的贡赋
senses.definition: a regular payment of goods or money by one state or people to a stronger one as an acknowledgment of dependence
senses.definitionCN: 一国或一族向更强者定期缴纳货物或钱财，以承认依附关系
senses.example: The province sent tribute every spring to the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 该省每年春天向都城进贡。
senses.why: Latin tributum was a thing contributed, from tribuere 'to allot', and the word starts as what is handed over on command.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 tributum 是被献出之物，出自 tribuere「分配」，因此这个词起初就是奉命交出之物。

senses.title: An offering expressing respect
senses.definition: a gift or act offered to show honour, gratitude or admiration
senses.definitionCN: 为表尊敬、感激或钦佩而献出的礼物或行为
senses.example: The village laid flowers as a tribute to the doctor who stayed.
senses.exampleCN: 村民献上鲜花，向留下来的那位医生致敬。
senses.why: What is given to a ruler under compulsion becomes, in free use, what is given to anyone out of respect.
senses.whyCN: 在强制之下交给统治者的东西，在自由的用法里就成了出于敬意交给任何人的东西。

senses.title: Evidence of a quality's worth
senses.definition: a visible proof of the excellence of something, as a tribute to a design or a method
senses.definitionCN: 某物之优良的可见证据，如对某种设计或方法的称许
senses.example: The bridge's survival is a tribute to the engineer who built it.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥得以存留，就是那位工程师的功劳证明。
senses.why: Praise is paid like a due, so an outcome that honours a maker is spoken of as a payment.
senses.whyCN: 赞誉像应缴之物一样被付出，因此为制作者增光的结果被说成一笔缴纳。

senses.title: A speech or ceremony in honour
senses.definition: a formal expression of praise, such as a eulogy, a memorial speech or a concert in someone's honour
senses.definitionCN: 正式的颂扬表达，如悼词、纪念演说或为某人举办的音乐会
senses.example: The concert was a tribute to the composer, not a performance of his music.
senses.exampleCN: 这场音乐会是对那位作曲家的致敬，并非演奏他的作品。
senses.why: A ceremony is the organised form of the offering, and the countable noun names the occasion.
senses.whyCN: 仪式是献礼的组织化形式，可数名词便指这一场合。

senses.title: Forced labour or goods exacted
senses.definition: historical: labour, produce or service exacted by a ruler or a landlord
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法：统治者或地主强征的劳役、产物或服务
senses.example: Ten days of tribute labour were owed to the lord each harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 每次收获，都要向领主服十天贡役。
senses.why: Where money is scarce, the same obligation is paid in work, and the noun covers the labour as well.
senses.whyCN: 在缺钱之处，同一种义务以劳动支付，而这个名词也涵盖劳动。

senses.title: A share of ore paid to the landowner
senses.definition: mining: a portion of ore or of its value paid to the owner of the ground as a condition of working it
senses.definitionCN: 矿业用法：作为开采条件付给地表所有者的一部分矿石或其价值
senses.example: The miners kept seven parts and gave one as tribute.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工留下七份，把一份作为矿产分成交出。
senses.why: The old duty on produce survives in one technical trade, attached to the ground rather than to a state.
senses.whyCN: 旧时对产物的义务在一个技术性行业中留存，付给土地而非国家。

senses.title: A levy in older English usage
senses.definition: archaic: a tax or levy imposed by a ruler or a town
senses.definitionCN: 古旧用法：由统治者或城镇课征的税或摊派
senses.example: The chronicle lists the tribute laid on each ward.
senses.exampleCN: 编年史记下了对每个街区摊派的款项。
senses.why: Before tax became the general word, tribute covered any exaction, and the older sense remains in historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 在 tax 成为通称之前，tribute 涵盖一切强征，这一旧义留在历史写作中。

senses.title: A tribute band or tribute act
senses.definition: a modern compound use for performers who imitate a famous artist as a form of homage
senses.definitionCN: 现代复合用法：以模仿某位名家来示敬的表演者
senses.example: The tribute band plays the same three albums note for note.
senses.exampleCN: 这支致敬乐队一个音不差地演奏那三张专辑。
senses.why: Imitation offered as honour is the same structure as goods offered to a superior, with admiration as the ruler.
senses.whyCN: 作为敬意献上的模仿，与献给尊长的货物是同一结构，只是把钦佩当作了尊者。

intro.en: Tribute comes from a Latin word for a thing assigned and handed over, and the same verb behind it builds contribute, distribute and attribute.
intro.cn: tribute 来自一个指「被分配并交出之物」的拉丁词，其背后的同一个动词还构成 contribute、distribute 与 attribute。

items.en: Tribus meant a tribe or a division of the Roman people, the unit through which taxes and duties were assigned. Its own origin is uncertain; a link to tri- 'three' is sometimes proposed but not demonstrated.
items.cn: tribus 指部族或罗马人民的划分单位，税赋正是通过这一单位摊派。它自身的来源不确定；有人提出与 tri-「三」的联系，但未得到证实。

items.en: Tribuere meant 'to allot, assign, grant, pay'. The verb starts from dividing among groups and ends by meaning to hand over what is owed.
items.cn: tribuere 意为「分配、指派、给予、支付」。这个动词从在群体间划分开始，最终指交出所欠之物。

items.en: Tributum was the thing contributed, a payment laid on a people; the neuter participle became a noun of the payment itself.
items.cn: tributum 是被献出之物，即摊在民众身上的缴纳；这个中性分词成了指缴纳本身的名词。

items.en: Old French tribut carries the payment sense into English, where it keeps the tone of obligation rather than of gift.
items.cn: 古法语 tribut 把缴纳义带入英语，在英语中保留了义务而非赠礼的语气。

items.en: The sense of an expression of respect develops in the sixteenth century, when praise is spoken of as something owed and paid.
items.cn: 表敬意的义项在十六世纪发展出来，当时赞誉被说成欠下并偿付之物。

items.en: Mining keeps the oldest sense as a share of ore for the landowner, while concert billing gives tribute a new life as an act of imitation offered in homage.
items.cn: 矿业把最古老的义项保留为付给地主的矿石分成，而演出海报又让 tribute 以「以模仿示敬」的方式获得新生。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb and is constantly confused; the second holds words for payments, praise and homage.
note.cn: 第一组共享那个拉丁动词，极易混淆；第二组是缴纳、赞誉与效忠的说法。

entries.definition: From tributarius 'paying tribute': a stream that feeds a larger river, as if paying it; it is also an adjective meaning subject to tribute.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 tributarius「缴纳贡赋的」：向大河供水的支流，仿佛在向它进贡；也可作形容词，指需纳贡的。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus tribuere: to give a share toward a common result, with no suggestion of submission.
entries.definitionCN: com-「共同」加 tribuere：为共同结果出一份力，不含臣服之意。

entries.definition: Ad- 'toward' plus tribuere: to assign a cause or a quality to something, which is to allot it.
entries.definitionCN: ad-「朝向」加 tribuere：把原因或性质指派给某物，也就是把它分配过去。

entries.definition: Re- 'back' plus tribuere: a paying back, hence punishment; it shares the verb but not the meaning of tribute.
entries.definitionCN: re-「回」加 tribuere：付还，因而指报应、惩罚；共享动词，但不共享 tribute 的词义。

entries.definition: A public acknowledgment of superiority or excellence, often ceremonial; tribute can be goods as well as words.
entries.definitionCN: 公开承认优越或卓越，常为仪式性的；tribute 既可以是言语，也可以是财物。

entries.definition: A charge imposed by authority; it names the raising, while tribute names what is handed over.
entries.definitionCN: 由当局课征的费用；它指征收行为，而 tribute 指交出的东西。

entries.definition: Something presented, often to a deity or a superior; it is typically voluntary, where tribute is typically owed.
entries.definitionCN: 呈献之物，常献给神或尊长；它通常出于自愿，而 tribute 通常是所欠。

entries.definition: A formal speech of praise, especially for the dead; it is one kind of tribute in sense four.
entries.definitionCN: 正式的颂扬演说，尤指悼词；它是第四个义项中 tribute 的一种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: tribuere 'to allot' + -tum 'thing done': the share assigned and handed over.
normal.cn: tribuere「分配」+ -tum「所做之物」：被指派并交出的那一份。

normal.en: The family runs tribute, tributary, contribute, contribution, distribute, attribute, retribution.
normal.cn: 同族词有 tribute、tributary、contribute、contribution、distribute、attribute、retribution。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: pay tribute to, annual tribute, a fitting tribute.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：向…致敬、年度贡赋、恰如其分的致敬。

normal.en: A river pays tribute to the sea: that is why a small stream is called a tributary.
normal.cn: 河向海进贡：这就是小水被称为支流的原因。

normal.en: The modern compound keeps the old structure: a tribute band offers imitation as homage.
normal.cn: 现代复合词保留旧结构：致敬乐队以模仿作献礼。

abstract.en: Picture a box opened at the foot of a throne, with the giver's head lower than the lid.
abstract.cn: 想象王座脚下打开的一只箱子，献者的头比箱盖还低。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge still standing after a century, quietly praising the hand that drew it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座百年后仍立着的桥，安静地称许画出它的那只手。

abstract.en: Picture miners counting out eight piles and pushing the ninth to the owner of the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象矿工数出八堆，把第九堆推到土地所有者面前。

examples.en: The empire demanded tribute in silver and in soldiers.
examples.cn: 帝国索取白银与兵员的贡赋。

examples.en: Her final book is a tribute to the teachers who doubted her.
examples.cn: 她最后一本书是向那些曾怀疑她的老师致敬。

examples.en: The miners paid tribute on every ton before they could sell the rest.
examples.cn: 矿工每吨都要先交分成，才能卖掉其余的。

dict_mnemonic.text: tribuere（分配、交出）→ 被交出的那一份；先记「王座前的木箱」，再记「以言代物的致敬」。

root: 拉丁 tribus（部族、划分单位）+ tribuere「分配、指派、支付」→ tributum「被献出之物」→ 古法语 tribut → 英语 tribute；tribus 更深来源不确定，与 tri-「三」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from a box at a throne to a band on a stage: the subject's payment, the offering of respect, the proof of worth, the ceremony of praise, exacted labour, a share of ore, an old levy, and imitation offered as homage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从王座前的一只箱子走到舞台上的一支乐队：属国的缴纳、表敬的献礼、价值的证明、颂扬的仪式、强征的劳役、矿石分成、旧时的课征，以及以模仿示敬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something valuable carried a long way and set down at the feet of someone stronger.
core.cn: 核心意象：贵重之物被抬了很远，放在更强者的脚下。

branches.en: WHAT IS OWED: payment in goods, payment in labour, and the older general levy are one obligation in three forms.
branches.cn: 所欠之物：以财物缴纳、以劳役缴纳、以及更早的泛称课征，是同一义务的三种形式。

branches.en: FROM DUTY TO HONOUR: an offering given under compulsion becomes a ceremony of respect freely staged.
branches.cn: 从义务到敬意：强制下的献礼变成自愿举行的致敬仪式。

branches.en: PRAISE AS PAYMENT: a lasting result is spoken of as something owed to its maker.
branches.cn: 以赞代付：长存的结果被说成欠其制作者的一笔账。

branches.en: THE GROUND'S SHARE: the same duty survives in mining, owed to a landowner rather than a state.
branches.cn: 土地的一份：同一义务在矿业留存，欠的是地主而非国家。

branches.en: IMITATION AS HOMAGE: copying a master well enough to honour him is the modern echo of carrying goods to a throne.
branches.cn: 以模仿示敬：把一位名家模仿到足以致敬，是把货物抬到王座前的现代回声。

intro.en: Tribute is the noun of a Latin verb of allotting, and that verb, not the noun, is what English borrowed again and again.
intro.cn: tribute 是一个表分配的拉丁动词的名词形式，而英语反复借入的是那个动词，不是这个名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribuere 'to allot' gives tribute, tributary, contribute, distribute, attribute and retribution, each with a different prefix; tribus 'tribe' is the unit behind the assigning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 tribuere「分配」给出 tribute、tributary、contribute、distribute、attribute 与 retribution，各自带不同前缀；tribus「部族」是分配背后的单位。

items.example: Taxes were assigned through these divisions.
items.exampleCN: 税赋正是通过这些划分单位摊派的。

items.example: The verb is the engine of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的发动机。

items.example: The participle became a noun of payment.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成了指缴纳的名词。

items.example: English keeps the obligation tone.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了义务的语气。

items.example: A small river is seen as paying tribute to a large one.
items.exampleCN: 小河被看作向大河进贡。

items.meaning: to give toward a common end
items.example: The prefix removes the idea of submission.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀去掉了臣服之意。

items.example: The noun is the everyday form of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是那个动词的日常形式。

items.example: The prefix spreads the allotting outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把分配向外铺开。

items.meaning: to assign as a cause or quality
items.example: Assigning a cause is a kind of allotting.
items.exampleCN: 归因也是一种指派。

items.example: The same verb reversed gives the opposite of a gift.
items.exampleCN: 同一个动词反向使用，给出赠礼的反面。

definition_zh: 诡计；把戏；窍门；戏弄；哄骗
definition_en: a clever act meant to deceive or amuse someone, or to deceive a person in that way
core_image: 一只手把硬币从这个人眼前晃过，却从那人耳后取出
scene: 街头围了一圈人，那个戴帽子的男人把手绢一晃，鸽子从袖口飞了出来。He knows a trick that makes a coin disappear.
sceneCN: 这里 trick 是「戏法、把戏」（第 2 个义项：逗人一乐的巧妙手法）；句意为他会一个让硬币消失的戏法。手一晃、东西换个地方出现，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -y 构成形容词，义为「棘手的；狡猾的」
名词加 -ery 构成，义为「欺骗行径」
名词加 -ster 构成，义为「骗子；恶作剧者」

senses.title: A plan to deceive someone
senses.definition: a clever but dishonest plan to get something from someone
senses.definitionCN: 巧妙却不老实、想从别人那里得利的计谋
senses.example: It was a trick to make him sign the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个骗他签字的诡计。
senses.why: The word comes from Old French trickier, to deceive, and its oldest sense is a cheat or a deceit.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自古法语 trickier（欺骗），最早的义项就是骗人或骗术。

senses.title: A clever act that amuses
senses.definition: a skilful performance, such as a card trick, done to entertain
senses.definitionCN: 为逗乐而做的熟练表演，如纸牌戏法
senses.example: The children loved the card trick.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们很喜欢那个纸牌戏法。
senses.why: A cheat and a magic show differ only in intent: both turn on a hidden method.
senses.whyCN: 骗人的手法与魔术表演只差用心：两者都靠一套藏着的方法。

senses.title: A clever way of doing something
senses.definition: a special way of doing a task that makes it easier
senses.definitionCN: 让事情变容易的特殊做法
senses.example: The trick is to stir the sauce slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 窍门是慢慢地搅酱汁。
senses.why: The hidden method that deceived someone can also simply help: then we call it the trick.
senses.whyCN: 那套藏着的方法如果不为骗人而是帮忙，我们就叫它窍门。

senses.title: To deceive someone
senses.definition: to make someone believe something untrue so that you gain an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 让人相信不实之事以取得好处
senses.example: They tricked him out of his savings.
senses.exampleCN: 他们骗走了他的存款。
senses.why: The verb is the act behind the noun: to work the hidden method on a person.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词背后的动作：把藏着的方法用在某个人身上。

senses.title: A habit or mannerism
senses.definition: a peculiar habit of speech or behaviour that a person is known for
senses.definitionCN: 某人为人熟知的言语或举止习惯
senses.example: He has a trick of raising one eyebrow.
senses.exampleCN: 他有个挑一挑眉的习惯。
senses.why: A repeated piece of behaviour becomes as automatic as a practised sleight.
senses.whyCN: 反复出现的小动作，会像练熟的手法一样成为本能。

intro.en: The word comes from Old French trique, a deceit or a cheat, and the verb trickier, to deceive.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 trique（欺骗、诈术）与动词 trickier（欺骗）。

items.en: Trique means a deceit, a shift, or a cheating play, and is used of dice and dealings.
items.cn: 古法语 trique 意为诈术、花招、骗人的把戏，用于骰子与交易。

items.en: English borrows the noun in the fifteenth century for a deceitful act.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个名词，指欺诈行为。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the word covers harmless sleight of hand and card play.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个词已涵盖无害的手法与纸牌戏法。

items.en: Later it names the clever knack of a trade and the odd habit of a person.
items.cn: 后来又用来指行业的技巧与一个人的怪癖。

items.en: The ultimate origin is uncertain; the word may be related to Old French trichier, to cheat.
items.cn: 最终来源不确定；可能和古法语 trichier（欺骗）有关。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words differing by one letter or sharing the stem, while the near-meaning group names other deceptions and knacks.
note.cn: 形近组汇集只差一个字母或共用词干的短词，近义组列出其他骗术与诀窍。

entries.definition: difficult or requiring care
entries.definitionCN: 棘手的；狡猾的

entries.definition: the use of tricks to deceive
entries.definitionCN: 欺骗；诈术

entries.definition: a large road vehicle
entries.definitionCN: 卡车

entries.definition: to flow in a thin slow stream
entries.definitionCN: 滴流；细流

entries.definition: a playful trick on someone
entries.definitionCN: 恶作剧

entries.definition: to make someone believe what is false
entries.definitionCN: 欺骗

entries.definition: a special skill at doing something
entries.definitionCN: 诀窍；本事

entries.definition: a false appearance made by a performer
entries.definitionCN: 幻象；错觉

normalIntro.en: Five letters, one sharp sound, and a family that grows from it.
normalIntro.cn: 五个字母，一个短促的音，还长出一整个词族。

normal.en: Tricky adds -y and means full of tricks, so difficult.
normal.cn: tricky 加 -y，意为满是机关，所以是棘手。

normal.en: Trickery adds -ery and names the practice of deceiving.
normal.cn: trickery 加 -ery，指欺骗的行径。

normal.en: A trickster is the person who plays the tricks.
normal.cn: trickster 就是耍弄这些把戏的人。

normal.en: Do the trick means the method works, with no deceit at all.
normal.cn: do the trick 指办法奏效，毫无欺骗之意。

normal.en: The verb takes a direct object and usually into: trick him into signing.
normal.cn: 这个动词带宾语，常加 into：trick him into signing。

abstract.en: Picture a coin leaving one palm and appearing behind an ear.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币离开一只手心，却出现在耳后。

abstract.en: Watch the empty palm open flat to prove nothing is there.
abstract.cn: 看那只空手摊平，证明什么也没有。

abstract.en: Then put that same sleight into a recipe and call it the trick.
abstract.cn: 再把这套手法放进菜谱里，就叫做窍门。

examples.en: The old trick of hiding a key under a flowerpot failed.
examples.cn: 把钥匙藏在花盆下这个老花招不管用了。

examples.en: It took me a while to learn the trick of folding the dough.
examples.cn: 我花了好一阵才学会折面团的窍门。

examples.en: They tricked the old man into paying twice.
examples.cn: 他们骗那位老人付了两次钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「踹克」——一脚踹开攻克对手的诡计，全靠手法。

root: 古法语 trique（诈术）与动词 trickier（欺骗），十五世纪进入英语；同族有 tricky、trickery、trickster，最终来源不确定

sensesIntro.en: One hidden method runs through every sense: it may cheat, amuse, help, or simply become a habit.
sensesIntro.cn: 一套藏着的方法贯穿所有义项：它可以骗人、逗乐、帮忙，或干脆变成一个习惯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coin that leaves one palm and appears elsewhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬币离开一只手心，在别处出现。

branches.en: The deceitful sense, where the method is used against someone.
branches.cn: 欺骗义：那套方法被用来对付人。

branches.en: The performing sense, where the method only entertains.
branches.cn: 表演义：那套方法只为逗乐。

branches.en: The helpful sense, where the same method makes work easy.
branches.cn: 助人义：同一套方法让活变简单。

branches.en: The verb sense, where the method is set in motion.
branches.cn: 动词义：把那套方法使出来。

branches.en: The habitual sense, where a mannerism repeats like a practised move.
branches.cn: 习惯义：小动作像练熟的手法一样重复。

intro.en: The word is short, but it builds a family with three productive suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词很短，却靠三个能产的词尾长出一族词。

latinIntro.en: The French source has no Latin relatives in English, so the Latin list here stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它的法语来源在英语里没有拉丁亲族，所以这里的拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: He played a trick on us.
items.exampleCN: 他捉弄了我们。

items.example: A tricky question caught everyone.
items.exampleCN: 一道棘手的题难住了所有人。

items.example: The deal was pure trickery.
items.exampleCN: 这笔交易纯属欺诈。

items.example: The trickster fooled the whole village.
items.exampleCN: 那个骗子骗了全村。

items.example: The path runs trickily downhill.
items.exampleCN: 这条小路刁钻地往山下走。

items.example: He underestimated the trickiness of the task.
items.exampleCN: 他低估了这件事的棘手程度。

items.meaning: a question designed to catch you
items.example: That was a trick question.
items.exampleCN: 那是个陷阱题。

items.example: The children shouted trick or treat.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们喊着不给糖就捣蛋。

items.example: The move looked tricky, even trickish.
items.exampleCN: 这一步看着就刁，甚至有点诡。

definition_zh: 触发；引发；激起；扳机；触发器；诱因
definition_en: to cause something to start suddenly, and the small lever or device that sets a mechanism going
core_image: 靶场上，一根手指搭在扳机上，只要一个很小的动作，整支枪的力量就会释放
scene: 靶场上，一根手指搭在扳机上，只要一个很小的动作，整支枪的力量就会释放。A single spark was enough to trigger the alarm.
sceneCN: 这里指引发、触发（第 1 个义项：使某事突然开始）；句意为一个火花就足以触发警报。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词的现在分词转成的名词或形容词，义为「触发；引发性的」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「被触发的；受激的」
由该名词与表示「热衷」的形容词合成为复合形容词，义为「动辄开枪的；莽撞行事的」
由该动词加表示可能性的形容词尾构成，义为「可被触发的」

senses.title: Cause an event to begin suddenly
senses.definition: to set off an event or a chain of events that would not have started by itself
senses.definitionCN: 使一个本不会自行开始的事件或连锁事件开始
senses.example: A small error can trigger a chain of failures.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小错误就可能引发一连串故障。
senses.why: The word began as the small lever that releases a gun, and the idea of a little act releasing a large force is the heart of every sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指释放枪械力量的小杠杆，而「一个小动作释放巨大力量」正是每个义项的核心。

senses.title: Provoke a strong feeling
senses.definition: to cause anger, fear or excitement in a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 引起个人或群体的愤怒、恐惧或激动
senses.example: The news triggered an angry response from the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 那条消息激起人群的愤怒回应。
senses.why: A feeling that was quiet suddenly fires, and the word pictures it as a mechanism released by a small event.
senses.whyCN: 原本安静的情绪突然开火，这个词把它画成被小事释放的机械。

senses.title: Set a device into operation
senses.definition: to make a sensor, circuit or machine begin working, often automatically
senses.definitionCN: 使传感器、电路或机器开始工作，常为自动进行
senses.example: The sensor triggers the lamp when someone walks past.
senses.exampleCN: 有人走过时，传感器就会触发那盏灯。
senses.why: This is the most literal modern sense: a small signal releases a larger action.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的现代义：一个小信号释放一个更大的动作。

senses.title: Induce an illness or symptom
senses.definition: in medicine, to cause a disease, attack or symptom to begin
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指引起疾病、发作或症状开始
senses.example: The virus can trigger a high fever.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒能引发高烧。
senses.why: A body already carrying a condition may need only one small provocation, and the word names that provocation.
senses.whyCN: 身体本就带着病因，也许只差一个很小的刺激，而这个词命名的正是那个刺激。

senses.title: The lever on a firearm
senses.definition: the small lever a finger pulls to fire a gun
senses.definitionCN: 手指扣动以使枪械击发的小杠杆
senses.example: He kept his finger off the trigger until the order came.
senses.exampleCN: 在命令下达之前，他的手指一直没有放在扳机上。
senses.why: This is the sense from which every other sense borrows its shape: the smallest part controls the largest release.
senses.whyCN: 这是其他所有义项借取形状的源头义：最小的部件控制最大的释放。

senses.title: An electronic pulse that starts an action
senses.titleCN: 电子触发器或触发脉冲
senses.definition: a signal in a circuit that tells another part to begin its cycle
senses.definitionCN: 电路中通知另一部件开始运行周期的信号
senses.example: The circuit sends a trigger to the camera every two seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 电路每隔两秒向相机发送一个触发信号。
senses.why: Electronics kept the gun image and made the lever invisible: a pulse instead of a finger.
senses.whyCN: 电子学保留了枪的意象，却把杠杆变得看不见：用脉冲代替手指。

senses.title: The cause or occasion of an event
senses.definition: the event or remark that was the immediate occasion for something larger
senses.definitionCN: 成为更大事件的直接起因的事件或言论
senses.example: The report was the trigger for a wider debate.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告成了更广泛争论的诱因。
senses.why: In this noun sense the lever becomes the occasion itself, the point at which the mechanism was released.
senses.whyCN: 在这个名词义项里，杠杆变成了事件本身，即机械被释放的那一刻。

senses.title: Bring a memory back
senses.definition: to cause a scene, smell or sound to bring an old memory into the mind
senses.definitionCN: 使景象、气味或声音把旧日记忆带回心中
senses.example: The smell of bread triggered a memory of his grandmother's kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 面包的气味唤起了他对祖母厨房的记忆。
senses.why: A memory sits loaded like a spring, and one small sensory cue can release it whole.
senses.whyCN: 记忆像上了弦的弹簧，一个小小的感官线索就能把它整个释放。

senses.title: Set off a biological response
senses.definition: to start an allergic, immune or inflammatory reaction in a living body
senses.definitionCN: 在生物体内引起过敏、免疫或炎症反应
senses.example: The pollen may trigger an allergic reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 花粉可能引发过敏反应。
senses.why: The body is the machine here, and the allergen is the finger on the lever.
senses.whyCN: 这里的机器是身体，而过敏原就是搭在杠杆上的那根手指。

intro.en: Trigger is a Dutch loan. It comes from trekker, a puller, from trekken, to pull, and it entered English first as a name for the lever of a firearm.
intro.cn: 这个词借自荷兰语，来自 trekker「拉者」，而 trekker 出自 trekken「拉」；它进入英语时最先指枪械上的杠杆。

items.en: Trekken meant to pull or draw, and it is also the source of the English word trek, a long journey drawn out by oxen.
items.cn: trekken 意为拉、拖，它也是英语 trek「长途跋涉」的来源，那正是牛车拉出来的路。

items.en: The noun meant one that pulls, and it could name a person, a rope or a part of a machine.
items.cn: 这个名词意为「拉的东西」，可以指人、指绳，也可以指机器部件。

items.en: The earliest English form was tricker, recorded in the sixteenth century for the lever of a gun; the spelling was not yet fixed.
items.cn: 最早的英语形式是 tricker，十六世纪时用来指枪的杠杆；当时拼写尚未固定。

items.en: The modern spelling settled in the seventeenth century, still tied to firearms before it moved to any small releasing part.
items.cn: 现代拼写在十七世纪固定下来，仍先与枪械绑定，之后才转向任何小的释放部件。

items.en: Machines and then circuits borrowed the word for any small part that starts a larger motion.
items.cn: 机器、随后是电路，都借这个词来指任何启动更大运动的细小部件。

items.en: Psychology and medicine extended it to memories, emotions and symptoms, where a small cue releases a large response.
items.cn: 心理学与医学把它扩展到记忆、情绪与症状，那里一个小小的线索就释放出很大的反应。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like trigger; the second group names neighbouring ways of starting something.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 trigger 相近；第二组是与「引发、启动」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The act of setting something off, or the quality of doing so.
entries.definitionCN: 指触发的行为，或指具有引发作用的性质。

entries.definition: Set off or activated by something else.
entries.definitionCN: 指被某物触发或激活的。

entries.definition: Too ready to shoot or to act rashly.
entries.definitionCN: 指动辄开枪或鲁莽行事的。

entries.definition: A large striped cat; it looks close in spelling but has no shared history.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种大型条纹猫科动物；拼写相近，但没有共同来源。

entries.definition: To flow in a thin stream; it sounds close but comes from a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指细细地流；读音相近，但来自另一个动词。

entries.definition: To make something happen; neutral about size and speed, and the broadest word here.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某事发生；不涉及大小与速度，是这里最宽泛的词。

entries.definition: To stir a feeling or a reaction, often deliberately; it stresses the irritation.
entries.definitionCN: 指激起情绪或反应，常含故意；强调被激起的恼怒。

entries.definition: To start something large from a very small beginning, with the image of a spark and dry grass.
entries.definitionCN: 指由极小的开端引发大事，意象是火星与干草。

entries.definition: To start a device, alarm or chain of events; plainer and more physical than trigger.
entries.definitionCN: 指启动装置、警报或一连串事件；比本词更朴素、更物理。

entries.definition: To begin something formally or deliberately, without the idea of a small lever.
entries.definitionCN: 指正式或有意地开始某事，不含「小杠杆」的意思。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the pulling root, the gun lever and the small-cause-large-effect pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用「拉」的词根、枪的杠杆，以及「小原因、大效果」的模式。

normal.en: The Dutch root means pull, so the trigger is the part you pull to release everything else.
normal.cn: 荷兰语词根意为拉，所以扳机就是你拉一下、其余一切随之释放的那个部件。

normal.en: A finger moves a few millimetres and the whole gun answers; that is the shape of the word.
normal.cn: 手指移动几毫米，整支枪都作出回应；这就是这个词的形状。

normal.en: A smoke detector is a trigger made electronic: a little smoke, a loud alarm.
normal.cn: 烟雾报警器就是电子化的扳机：一点烟，一阵大响。

normal.en: A smell that brings back a kitchen is the same mechanism working on memory.
normal.cn: 让厨房重现的气味，是同一套机械在记忆上工作。

normal.en: The stock phrase pull the trigger keeps the original object visible inside the modern verb.
normal.cn: 固定说法「扣动扳机」让原本的物件在现代动词里仍然可见。

abstract.en: A trigger is defined by the ratio between the small input and the large release.
abstract.cn: 扳机的本质，在于小输入与大释放之间的比例。

abstract.en: The same event can be a trigger for one person and a trifle for another, because the mechanism is inside.
abstract.cn: 同一件事对一个人是扳机，对另一个人却无关紧要，因为机械装在内部。

abstract.en: Naming a trigger is already a way of taking some power back from it.
abstract.cn: 说出一个触发点，本身已经是从它手里收回一部分权力。

examples.en: The ruling triggered protests across the country.
examples.cn: 那项裁决引发了全国范围的抗议。

examples.en: A loud noise can trigger a panic attack.
examples.cn: 巨大的声响可能引发惊恐发作。

examples.en: The alarm was triggered by a broken wire.
examples.cn: 警报是被一根断线触发的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「吹格」——手指一「吹」，扳机一「格」响，整支枪就响了：扳机、触发

root: 荷兰语 trekken「拉」→ trekker「拉者、拉动的部件」→ 英语早期形式 tricker（十六世纪指枪的杠杆）→ trigger「扳机」→ 动词「触发、引发」；核心是「一个很小的拉动释放很大的力量」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all follow one pattern, a small act releasing a large response: events, feelings, devices, illness, the gun lever itself, circuits, occasions, memories and allergic reactions.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都遵循同一个模式——小动作释放大反应：事件、情绪、装置、疾病、枪的杠杆本身、电路、诱因、记忆与过敏反应。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one finger on a small lever, and the whole weapon answers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指搭在小杠杆上，整件武器随之响应。

branches.en: THE RELEASE BRANCH: one error starts a chain, and one allergen starts a reaction.
branches.cn: 释放分支：一个错误引发连锁，一个过敏原引发反应。

branches.en: THE INNER BRANCH: a piece of news fires anger, and a smell fires a memory.
branches.cn: 内部分支：一条消息点燃愤怒，一种气味点燃记忆。

branches.en: THE MACHINE BRANCH: a sensor starts a lamp, and a pulse starts a camera.
branches.cn: 机械分支：传感器启动灯，脉冲启动相机。

branches.en: THE ILLNESS BRANCH: a virus provokes a fever in a body already carrying it.
branches.cn: 疾病分支：病毒在本已带病的身体里诱发高烧。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN BRANCH: the gun lever itself, and the occasion that releases a debate.
branches.cn: 源头分支：枪的杠杆本身，以及释放一场争论的诱因。

intro.en: Trigger is not a Latin word at all: it is a Dutch loan whose parts are a verb of pulling and an agent ending.
intro.cn: 这个词根本不是拉丁词，而是一个荷兰语借词，其部件是一个表示「拉」的动词和一个施动词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin etymon behind this word. Its family is Germanic, and the Latin entries are therefore left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁语词源，它属于日耳曼语族，因此拉丁语条目留空。

items.example: The pulling action is the physical core of the word.
items.exampleCN: 「拉」这个动作是这个词的物理核心。

items.example: It turns the verb into a noun for the thing that pulls.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成指「拉动之物」的名词。

items.example: The Dutch noun named the part that sets a mechanism going.
items.exampleCN: 这个荷兰语名词命名启动机械的那个部件。

items.example: English took the Dutch noun and narrowed it to the gun part.
items.exampleCN: 英语借入这个荷兰语名词，并把意义收窄到枪的部件。

items.structure: English conversion from noun to verb
items.example: English turned the part into an action without adding an ending.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个部件直接变成动作，没有加任何词尾。

items.example: The compound keeps the gun sense alive in ordinary speech.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词让枪的义项在日常说法里继续存活。

items.example: It forms triggered, the past and participle of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 triggered，即该动词的过去式与过去分词。

items.meaning: ongoing action, or the act itself
items.meaningCN: 正在进行的动作，或行为本身
items.example: It forms triggering, both participle and verbal noun.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 triggering，既是分词也是动名词。

derivatives.zh: 由该动词的现在分词转成的名词或形容词，义为「触发；引发性的」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「被触发的；受激的」
由该名词与表示「热衷」的形容词合成为复合形容词，义为「动辄开枪的；莽撞行事的」
由该动词加表示可能性的形容词尾构成，义为「可被触发的」

definition_zh: 修剪；整理；削减；整齐的；修长的
definition_en: to cut a small amount from something to make it neat, or to reduce an amount; neat and well shaped
core_image: 一把剪刀沿着边线走一圈，多出来的毛边落在地上
scene: 花园里，园丁拿长剪沿着绿篱一路剪过去，剪口平得像一条线。He trims the hedge every Saturday morning.
sceneCN: 这里 trim 是「修剪」（第 1 个义项：剪去多余部分使其整齐）；句意为他每周六早上修剪绿篱。剪刀沿线走、毛边落地的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 现在分词名词化，义为「修剪；装饰边；配料」
动词加 -er 构成，义为「修剪者；修剪工具」
形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「整齐；整洁」

senses.title: To cut something neat
senses.definition: to cut a small amount off something so that it looks tidy
senses.definitionCN: 剪掉一点使某物看起来整齐
senses.example: She trimmed the rose bushes back.
senses.exampleCN: 她把玫瑰丛修剪了一遍。
senses.why: The old verb means to make ready or to arrange, and neat cutting is the way such arranging is done.
senses.whyCN: 这个古动词意为「整理、备好」，而剪整齐正是整理的做法。

senses.title: To reduce an amount
senses.definition: to make a sum, a list, or a text smaller by removing parts
senses.definitionCN: 去掉一部分，使金额、清单或文字变小
senses.example: The council trimmed the spending plan.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会削减了开支计划。
senses.why: Cutting a hedge and cutting a budget are the same motion: taking off what sticks out.
senses.whyCN: 剪树篱与削预算都是同一个动作：把多出来的部分去掉。

senses.title: To decorate an edge
senses.definition: to add a border or ornament to the edge of something
senses.definitionCN: 在某物的边上加饰边或装饰
senses.example: The dress is trimmed with lace.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子镶了花边。
senses.why: The word also meant to fit out or equip, and decorating an edge is part of that outfitting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也曾表示装配、置办，而给边镶饰正是装配的一部分。

senses.title: Neat and well shaped
senses.definition: looking neat, slim, and in good order
senses.definitionCN: 看起来整洁、匀称、有精神
senses.example: He keeps a trim little garden.
senses.exampleCN: 他把小花园打理得很整齐。
senses.why: What has been trimmed looks trim: the adjective is the result of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 被修剪过的东西显得整齐：形容词就是动词的结果。

senses.title: To adjust the balance of a boat
senses.definition: to arrange the load or sails of a boat so that it sits level
senses.definitionCN: 调整船的负载或帆，使船身平稳
senses.example: The crew trimmed the sails before the wind rose.
senses.exampleCN: 风起前船员调好了帆。
senses.why: Balancing a boat is tidying a different edge, so the same word serves on water.
senses.whyCN: 给船找平是在整理另一条边，于是同一个词也用在水上。

intro.en: The verb is an old English word for making ready or arranging, and neat cutting is its oldest surviving sense.
intro.cn: 这个动词是古英语里表示准备、整理的老词，剪整齐是它保存下来的最早义项。

items.en: Trymman means to make firm, to strengthen, or to arrange a thing.
items.cn: 古英语 trymman 意为使牢固、增强，或把事物安排好。

items.en: The word narrows towards tidying edges, and is used of hair, cloth, and hedges.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐收窄到整理边缘，用于头发、布料与树篱。

items.en: Commerce gives it the sense of cutting down a sum or a staff.
items.cn: 商业给了它削减金额或人员的义项。

items.en: Nautical use keeps an older sense of setting a load or sail in balance.
items.cn: 航海用法保留了「把负载或帆调平衡」的较老义项。

items.en: The adjective grows from the noun, naming what has just been made neat.
items.cn: 形容词由名词生出，用来指刚被弄整齐的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short words close in spelling or root, while the near-meaning group names other cuts and states of neatness.
note.cn: 形近组汇集拼写或词根相近的短词，近义组列出其他剪切与整洁状态。

entries.definition: a journey or a stumble
entries.definitionCN: 旅行；绊倒

entries.definition: the outer edge of something
entries.definitionCN: 边缘；外缘

entries.definition: a tool or person that trims
entries.definitionCN: 修剪工具；修剪者

entries.definition: to shake slightly
entries.definitionCN: 发抖；只是开头写法相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to cut back branches
entries.definitionCN: 修剪枝条

entries.definition: to cut a small piece off
entries.definitionCN: 剪下；修剪

entries.definition: tidy and in good order
entries.definitionCN: 整洁的

entries.definition: thin in an attractive way
entries.definitionCN: 苗条的

normalIntro.en: Think of the barber’s shop and of a budget: the same short word cuts both.
normalIntro.cn: 想想理发店与预算：同一个短词，两边都能剪。

normal.en: The past tense doubles the m: trimmed.
normal.cn: 过去式双写 m：trimmed。

normal.en: Trimmer is the tool or the person, trimming is the cut-off pieces.
normal.cn: trimmer 是工具或人，trimming 是剪下来的碎料。

normal.en: Trim the hedge, trim the budget, and trim the sails all mean tidy an edge.
normal.cn: 剪树篱、削预算、调帆，都是在整理一条边。

normal.en: In trim means in good condition, especially of a body or a boat.
normal.cn: in trim 指状态良好，尤其指身材或船。

normal.en: The adjective and the verb share one spelling.
normal.cn: 形容词与动词拼写完全相同。

abstract.en: Hear the snip of shears running along a straight hedge.
abstract.cn: 听长剪沿着笔直的树篱一路咔嚓。

abstract.en: See the green bits fall and the top become a line.
abstract.cn: 看绿屑落下，顶面变成一条线。

abstract.en: Then hold the same shears over a sheet of numbers.
abstract.cn: 再把同一把剪子悬在一张数字表上。

examples.en: Could you trim a little off the back, please?
examples.cn: 后面能帮我修掉一点吗？

examples.en: The firm trimmed fifty jobs from the plant.
examples.cn: 公司从厂里削减了五十个岗位。

examples.en: The boat looked trim and ready for the race.
examples.cn: 这条船看起来整洁挺括，随时能比赛。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹姆」——对着刘海吹一口，再拿剪子修整齐。

root: 古英语 trymman（使牢固、整理），后收窄为「修剪边缘」；同族有 trimming、trimmer、trimness

sensesIntro.en: The senses all start from tidying an edge, then spread to money, ornament, appearance, and balance.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项都从「整理边缘」出发，再扩到钱、饰边、外形与平衡。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: shears running along a hedge, leaving a straight line.
core.cn: 核心意象：长剪沿着树篱走，留下一条直线。

branches.en: The cutting sense, where an edge is made neat.
branches.cn: 修剪义：把边剪整齐。

branches.en: The reducing sense, where a sum is cut down.
branches.cn: 削减义：把数字剪小。

branches.en: The decorating sense, where an edge is dressed.
branches.cn: 装饰义：给边加打扮。

branches.en: The adjective and the nautical senses, where the result is order and balance.
branches.cn: 形容词与航海义：结果是秩序与平衡。

branches.en: The hedge sense again, where the shears do the tidying.
branches.cn: 再回修剪义：干这份活的是长剪。

intro.en: The word is short and Germanic, and its suffixes are the common English ones.
intro.cn: 这个词短小且属日耳曼语，词尾都是常见的英语词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin relative in English, so the Latin list here stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 它在英语里没有拉丁亲族，所以这里的拉丁同源词留空。

items.example: Trim the edges with a knife.
items.exampleCN: 用刀把边修一修。

items.example: Trim becomes trimmed.
items.exampleCN: trim 加它成为 trimmed。

items.example: Trim gives trimming.
items.exampleCN: trim 加它成为 trimming。

items.example: Trim gives trimmer.
items.exampleCN: trim 加它成为 trimmer。

items.example: Trim gives trimness.
items.exampleCN: trim 加它成为 trimness。

items.meaning: keeps the short vowel before a suffix
items.meaningCN: 词尾加缀时双写辅音以保短元音
items.example: Trim gives trimmed in the past, not trimed.
items.exampleCN: trim 的过去式是 trimmed，不是 trimed。

items.example: Serve with all the trimmings.
items.exampleCN: 配上全套配菜端上桌。

items.example: The garden was trimly kept.
items.exampleCN: 花园打理得整整齐齐。

items.example: The untrimmed hedge blocked the path.
items.exampleCN: 没修剪的树篱把路挡住了。

definition_zh: 旅行；旅程；绊倒；（药物引起的）迷幻体验
definition_en: a journey to a place and back, especially a short one, or an act of catching your foot and stumbling
core_image: 一列小火车似的巴士沿山路开进雾里，车窗上映着笑脸
scene: 周末清晨，一群人背着包上了开往山里的巴士。We took a trip to the mountains and stayed for two nights.
sceneCN: 这里 trip 是「旅行；旅程」（第 1 个义项：去某地再回来的行程，尤指短途）；句意为我们去山里旅行，住了两晚。清晨背包装车的那群人，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 trip 加 -er 构成，义为「（短途）游客」
由 trip 加 -ing 构成，义为「轻快的（步伐）」
以 tri-（三）构成，义为「三脚架」

senses.title: Out and back
senses.definition: a journey to a place, especially a short one that ends at home
senses.definitionCN: 到某地的一次行程，尤指以回家告终的短途
senses.example: We took a trip to the mountains and stayed for two nights.
senses.exampleCN: 我们去山里旅行了一趟，住了两晚。
senses.why: The word may come from an old verb for skipping, because a short journey is a lively hop out and back.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可能源自意为「轻跳」的旧动词，因为短途出行就是轻快地跳出再回来。

senses.title: The foot catches
senses.definition: to catch your foot on something and lose balance
senses.definitionCN: 脚被某物挡住而失去平衡
senses.example: He tripped over the edge of the carpet.
senses.exampleCN: 他被地毯的边角绊了一下。
senses.why: A hop that goes wrong becomes a stumble, and this literal sense still lives in the verb.
senses.whyCN: 跳得不好就成了踉跄，这一字面含义仍留在动词里。

senses.title: Setting something off
senses.definition: to cause a switch or a machine to start working
senses.definitionCN: 使开关或机器开始运作
senses.example: A loose wire tripped the alarm at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一根松动的电线在半夜触发了警报。
senses.why: A light foot catches a lever, and the mechanism starts, so machines also get tripped.
senses.whyCN: 轻脚一碰钩住杠杆，机构便启动，于是机器也会被 trip。

senses.title: A single outbound turn
senses.definition: one leg of a journey, counted as a single unit
senses.definitionCN: 行程中的一段，按一个单位计数
senses.example: The truck made four trips between the quarry and the site.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车在采石场和工地之间跑了四趟。
senses.why: When journeys are counted, each single run out and back becomes one trip by itself.
senses.whyCN: 当行程被计数时，每一趟出去再回来本身就成了一次 trip。

intro.en: Trip is a short English word of uncertain origin, probably connected with old verbs for skipping and stumbling.
intro.cn: trip 是来源不确定的短小英语词，可能与表示跳跃与踉跄的旧动词有关。

items.en: No sure source is known; it appears in the Middle English period as a verb of light movement.
items.cn: 确切来源不明；它在中古英语时期已作为表示轻快动作的动词出现。

items.en: To trippen meant to step lightly, and also to stumble on a stone.
items.cn: trippen 意为轻步走，也指在石头上踉跄。

items.en: A short sea voyage was called a trip in the early modern period.
items.cn: 近代早期，一段短途海上航程被称作 a trip。

items.en: By the nineteenth century a trip covered any short journey by train or coach.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，trip 已指任何乘火车或马车的短途行程。

items.en: The machine sense, tripping a switch, grew out of the same light touch.
items.cn: 触发开关的机械义同样出自那次轻碰。

note.en: The first group shares the trip stem and sound, the second holds words for journeys and stumbles.
note.cn: 第一组共享 trip 的词干与读音，第二组收表示旅程与踉跄的词。

entries.definition: A person on a short trip.
entries.definitionCN: 短途游客

entries.definition: Moving lightly or catching the foot.
entries.definitionCN: 轻快行进的；绊着的

entries.definition: Stumbled or set off a device.
entries.definitionCN: 绊倒了；触发了

entries.definition: Travel from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 旅程；行程

entries.definition: A short pleasure trip with others.
entries.definitionCN: 出游；远足

entries.definition: To catch the foot and nearly fall.
entries.definitionCN: 绊跌；踉跄

normalIntro.en: Trip is a tiny word with two lives: a small hop out somewhere, and a small hop that goes wrong.
normalIntro.cn: trip 这个词很小，却有两重生活：轻快地跳出去一趟，以及轻跳失手的一下。

normal.en: Take a trip means go out and come back.
normal.cn: take a trip 意为出去再回来。

normal.en: Past forms double the p: tripped, tripping.
normal.cn: 过去式双写 p：tripped、tripping。

normal.en: Trip over is the everyday stumble phrase.
normal.cn: trip over 是日常的绊倒说法。

normal.en: The plural simply adds s: trips.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s：trips。

normal.en: Tripper turns the word into a person.
normal.cn: tripper 把这个词变成一个人。

abstract.en: A duffel bag by the door on a Friday night.
abstract.cn: 周五晚上门口的一只行李包。

abstract.en: A stone on a path you did not look at.
abstract.cn: 路上你没留意的一块石头。

abstract.en: A light foot catching a wire and waking the alarm.
abstract.cn: 轻脚绊到一根线，把警报唤醒。

examples.en: The bus leaves before dawn for a day trip to the lake.
examples.cn: 去湖边一日游的大巴在天亮前出发。

examples.en: She tripped on the last stair and dropped her keys.
examples.cn: 她在最后一级台阶绊了一下，钥匙掉在地上。

examples.en: Our trip to the coast was cut short by the storm.
examples.cn: 我们的海边之行被暴风雨提前中断。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「吹蒲」——吹着蒲公英去旅行；脚下一绊，就是 trip 的另一义。

root: 来源不确定（中古英语 trippen 意为轻步走、踉跄），近代扩展出「短途旅行」与「触发装置」两义；同族词有 tripper、tripping、tripped。

sensesIntro.en: First the short journey, then the stumble, then the small touch that sets a device going.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是短途旅行，再是踉跄，最后是那点轻碰把装置启动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bag by the door and a stone on the path.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口的行囊与路上的一块石头。

branches.en: The journey branch: a short way out and back.
branches.cn: 旅程分支：短程出去再回来。

branches.en: The body branch: a foot catching and slipping.
branches.cn: 身体分支：脚绊住并滑开。

branches.en: The mechanism branch: a light touch starts a machine.
branches.cn: 机械分支：轻轻一碰让机器启动。

branches.en: The hop branch: both grew from a light skip.
branches.cn: 跳跃分支：两者都出自轻跳。

branches.en: The trigger branch: feet and levers both catch.
branches.cn: 触发分支：脚与杠杆都会被钩住。

intro.en: Trip is a free stem of uncertain origin that easily takes endings such as -er and -ing.
intro.cn: trip 是来源不明的自由词干，可以方便地加上 -er、-ing 等词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the journey words below, which are cousins rather than direct ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 下面的旅程词汇出自拉丁语，它们只是远亲而非直接祖先。

items.example: The stem also works as a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干也能作动词。

items.example: It forms tripper, a short-trip visitor.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tripper，短途游客。

items.example: It forms tripping, moving lightly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tripping，轻快行进的。

items.example: Two trips in one month were too many.
items.exampleCN: 一个月两次旅行太多了。

items.example: The p doubles before the ending.
items.exampleCN: 加词尾前 p 要双写。

items.example: Day fixes the length of the outing.
items.exampleCN: day 限定了出游的长度。

items.example: Business names the reason for the journey.
items.exampleCN: business 说明出行的理由。

items.example: The same letters open a word about three feet.
items.exampleCN: 同样的字母开头，构成了关于三只脚的词。

definition_zh: 微不足道的；琐碎的；轻微的；（数学）平凡的；浅薄的
definition_en: of little importance or value, or so simple that it needs no special effort
core_image: 会议桌一端堆着修改用词的纸条，另一端那份预算缺口表始终没人翻开
scene: 会议开了半小时，大家还在争表格里一个无关紧要的用词，真正的预算缺口没人提。The committee spent an hour on a trivial wording issue while the budget gap went unmentioned.
sceneCN: 这里指重要性很小、不值得花时间（第 1 个义项：微不足道的）；句意为委员会花一小时争一个无关紧要的用词，预算缺口却无人提及。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、修改用词的纸条、预算缺口表、翻开的文件夹。

pos.zh: 微不足道的；琐碎的；浅薄的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「琐碎；微不足道的事」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「微不足道地；平凡地」
由该形容词加动词尾构成，义为「使显得琐碎；轻描淡写」
由「使显得琐碎」加名词尾构成，义为「淡化；琐碎化」
由拉丁语「三岔路」构成，义为中世纪的三门基础学科
由同一拉丁词的中性复数构成，义为「琐事；冷知识」

senses.title: Of little importance
senses.definition: too small or unimportant to affect the main matter
senses.definitionCN: 太小或不重要，影响不到主要问题
senses.example: The delay was trivial compared with the cost of a wrong decision.
senses.exampleCN: 与错误决策的代价相比，这点延误微不足道。
senses.why: The word's history runs from the crossroads to the common, and then to the common that no longer matters.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的历史从「三岔路口」走到「平常」，再走到「平常到不再重要」。

senses.title: An everyday trifle
senses.definition: a small everyday detail hardly worth attention
senses.definitionCN: 不值得关注的小日常细节
senses.example: They argued about whose turn it was to water the plants, a trivial matter in a busy week.
senses.exampleCN: 他们争该轮到谁浇花，这在忙碌的一周里只是琐事。
senses.why: A matter is trivial when its size, not its difficulty, is the reason to ignore it.
senses.whyCN: 一件事被称为琐事，是因为它小，而不是因为它难。

senses.title: A cost too small to count
senses.definition: an expense so small that it does not change a decision
senses.definitionCN: 小到不会改变决策的支出
senses.example: The extra licence fee is trivial next to the legal risk.
senses.exampleCN: 与法律风险相比，额外的许可费微不足道。
senses.why: Costs are trivial when the decision would be the same without them.
senses.whyCN: 成本在去掉它决策也不变时，就是微不足道的。

senses.title: The obvious solution in mathematics
senses.definition: the simple solution that satisfies the equation without special work, often zero
senses.definitionCN: 无需特别处理即满足方程的简单解，常为零
senses.example: The equation has a trivial solution at zero and two others that matter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程有一个位于零的平凡解，另有两个真正重要的解。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the word for the case that gives itself away, which is the technical descendant of commonplace.
senses.whyCN: 数学用它指那个自己送上门的情形，是「平常」这一义的技术后裔。

senses.title: An objection that misses the point
senses.definition: a complaint that does not touch the main question
senses.definitionCN: 没有触及主要问题的抱怨
senses.example: He raised a trivial objection about the font and said nothing about the data.
senses.exampleCN: 他对字体提了个无关紧要的反对，对数据却一言不发。
senses.why: An objection is trivial when it leaves the main claim standing.
senses.whyCN: 反对在主要主张仍然立得住时，就是无关紧要的。

senses.title: Small details used to avoid the issue
senses.definition: minor points brought up to delay or distract
senses.definitionCN: 用细小的点来拖延或转移注意
senses.example: The report drowns in trivial details and never states the cause.
senses.exampleCN: 报告淹没在细枝末节里，始终没说清原因。
senses.why: Details become trivial when they are used to fill the space where the argument should be.
senses.whyCN: 当细节被用来填满本该放论证的位置，它们就成了细枝末节。

senses.title: Shallow talk
senses.definition: conversation without substance or interest
senses.definitionCN: 没有实质或趣味的谈话
senses.example: The party talk was trivial, but it passed the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会上的谈话很浅薄，却也把晚上打发了。
senses.why: Talk without substance earns the word because it leaves nothing behind.
senses.whyCN: 没有实质的谈话得到这个词，因为它什么也没留下。

senses.title: A minor fault
senses.definition: an offence treated as slight rather than serious
senses.definitionCN: 被当作轻微而非严重的过错
senses.example: Under the old rules, a late form was a trivial offence with no penalty.
senses.exampleCN: 按旧规，迟交表格属轻微过失，不受处罚。
senses.why: Law calls a fault trivial when the penalty is lighter than the paperwork.
senses.whyCN: 当处罚比文书手续还轻时，法律就把该过失称为轻微的。

senses.title: Too simple to need comment
senses.definition: so easy in computing or logic that it is not worth explaining
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机或逻辑上简单到不值得解释
senses.example: The remaining case is trivial, so the proof simply says it follows.
senses.exampleCN: 剩下的情形简单到无需说明，证明里只写一句「由此可得」。
senses.why: The technical sense keeps the oldest idea: so common and easy that it needs no remark.
senses.whyCN: 技术义保留了最古老的意思：太寻常、太容易，因而不必再提。

intro.en: Trivial comes from Latin trivialis, belonging to the crossroads, from trivium, a place where three roads meet. Medieval schools called the first three arts the trivium, so the adjective meant belonging to the basic studies, then commonplace, and finally of little importance. The modern sense grew out of that social judgement rather than from the number three.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示「属于三岔路的」形容词，出自表示「三条路交汇处」的名词。中世纪学校把最初三门学科称为「三艺」，形容词于是指「属于基础学科的」，再变成「平常的」，最后成为「不重要的」。现代义从这种社会判断长出来，而不是从数字「三」直接得来。

items.en: A trivium was a place where three roads met, from tri- three and via road.
items.cn: 这个词指三条路交汇之处，由「三」与「道路」构成。

items.en: The adjective meant belonging to such a public corner, hence common and ordinary.
items.cn: 该形容词指属于这种人流交汇的公共角落，因此有「平常、普通」之意。

items.en: The first three liberal arts were called the trivium, and trivialis came to mean belonging to basic instruction.
items.cn: 最初三门博雅学科合称「三艺」，形容词于是指「属于基础教学的」。

items.en: English took the word for things common and therefore slight.
items.cn: 英语把这个词用于平常因而轻贱的事物。

items.en: The sense of unimportant hardened, and mathematics adopted it for the obvious case.
items.cn: 「不重要」义渐趋固定，数学又用它指显然的情形。

items.en: Quiz games and computing gave the word new phrases; the first date of each is uncertain.
items.cn: 问答游戏与计算机给出新的说法；各自首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the crossroads root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of smallness. The note also ties trivial to its noun triviality.
note.cn: 第一组共享「三岔路」词根或形近；第二组指其他「小」的说法。这里也把形容词与其名词形式「琐碎」连起来。

entries.definition: The quality of being trivial, or a trivial thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指微不足道的性质，或一件琐事。

entries.definition: In a way that is easy or unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 指以轻易或不重要的方式。

entries.definition: To make something serious seem trivial.
entries.definitionCN: 指把严肃的事说得微不足道。

entries.definition: The three basic arts of the medieval curriculum.
entries.definitionCN: 指中世纪课程里的三门基础学科。

entries.definition: Small facts and unimportant details.
entries.definitionCN: 指小而无关紧要的事实与细节。

entries.definition: Hard labour or painful effort; it comes from a word for a three-pronged tool, not from the crossroads.
entries.definitionCN: 指艰苦劳作或痛苦努力；出自指三齿工具的词，与三岔路无关。

entries.definition: Too small to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 指小到不值得考虑。

entries.definition: Small and unimportant, often said with a slight reproach.
entries.definitionCN: 指小而不重要，常带轻微责备。

entries.definition: Smaller in size, rank or importance than others.
entries.definitionCN: 指在规模、位次或重要性上较小。

entries.definition: So small that it can be ignored in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指小到实践中可以忽略。

entries.definition: Small-minded or concerned with small matters.
entries.definitionCN: 指心胸窄或只在意小事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the crossroads, the basic school subjects, the meeting that argues about wording, and the obvious equation case.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用三岔路口、基础学科、为一个用词争吵的会议，以及显然的方程情形。

normal.en: A crossroads is public and common, and common things soon look small.
normal.cn: 三岔路是公共而平常的，而平常的东西很快就显得微小。

normal.en: The three basic arts were the trivium, so trivial once meant elementary, not worthless.
normal.cn: 三门基础学科合称三艺，所以这个词曾经意为「基础的」，而不是「无价值的」。

normal.en: A trivial solution is the one that offers itself without effort.
normal.cn: 平凡解就是那个不用费力自己送上门的解。

normal.en: A trivial objection changes the font, not the argument.
normal.cn: 无关紧要的反对改的是字体，不是论证。

normal.en: Triviality is what happens when a serious subject is discussed only in small details.
normal.cn: 琐碎化，就是严肃话题只剩细枝末节时发生的事。

abstract.en: Calling something trivial is a way of deciding what will not be looked at.
abstract.cn: 把某事称为微不足道，是在决定什么不必再看。

abstract.en: The crossroads made a word for the common, and the common became a verdict on worth.
abstract.cn: 「三岔路」造出了一个表示「平常」的词，而「平常」又变成了对价值的判决。

abstract.en: Every field keeps a set of trivial cases, and they are the ones that teach the shape of the rest.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都留着一批平凡情形，而正是它们教人看清其余部分的形状。

examples.en: The difference in price is trivial compared with the difference in quality.
examples.cn: 与质量差距相比，价格差距微不足道。

examples.en: Do not waste the meeting on trivial details that the report already covers.
examples.cn: 别把会议浪费在报告里已经写到的细枝末节上。

examples.en: The first case is trivial, so the proof moves straight to the second.
examples.cn: 第一种情形简单到无需说明，所以证明直接转向第二种。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「吹尾偶」：三岔路口人来人往，人人都聊的「小事」，风一「吹」就散了

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「三岔路口」的名词，由「三」与「道路」构成，派生形容词义为「属于三岔路的、平常的」。中世纪把三门基础学科合称三艺，于是又指「基础学科的」，再演变为「平常的」，最后成为「微不足道的」。数学「平凡解」义为十九世纪后的技术引申；各短语首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from the crossroads to the equation: unimportant, an everyday trifle, a negligible cost, the obvious mathematical case, a pointless objection, distracting details, shallow talk, a slight fault, and the simple case that needs no comment.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从三岔路走到方程：不重要、日常琐事、可忽略的成本、数学的显然情形、无的放矢的反对、转移注意的细节、浅薄的闲谈、轻微过失，以及无需说明的简单情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one end of the table is covered with notes about wording, while the budget sheet stays shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌子一端堆满改词的纸条，另一端的预算表始终没有翻开。

branches.en: THE SMALL AMOUNT: importance and cost measured and found tiny.
branches.cn: 微小的分量：重要性与成本一量就小。

branches.en: THE TRIFLE AND THE DISTRACTION: small items, and small items used to avoid the point.
branches.cn: 琐事与分神：小东西，以及被用来回避要点的小东西。

branches.en: THE EASY CASE: the solution or case that offers itself.
branches.cn: 轻易的情形：自己送上门的解或情形。

branches.en: THE LIGHT COMPLAINT: an objection or fault too slight to matter.
branches.cn: 轻微的抱怨：轻到不必计较的反对或过失。

branches.en: THE SHALLOW TALK: conversation without substance.
branches.cn: 浅薄的谈话：没有实质的闲聊。

intro.en: Trivial is a crossroads noun with an adjective ending; the family covers trivia, the three basic arts, and the act of making something seem small.
intro.cn: 这个词是「三岔路」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖冷知识、三门基础学科，以及「把某事说得微不足道」的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin tri- and via build trivium, and the derived adjective trivialis supplies the English word and its whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「三」与「道路」构成表示「三岔路」的名词，派生形容词给出英语词及其整个词族。

items.example: It marks the meeting of three roads.
items.exampleCN: 它标出三条路的交汇。

items.example: It is also the source of English via.
items.exampleCN: 它也是英语「经由」的来源。

items.example: The noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这是整个词族背后的名词。

items.example: It gives the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It marks the word as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把该词标为形容词。

items.example: It forms triviality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「琐碎」。

items.example: It forms trivialize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「使显得琐碎」。

items.example: The plural keeps the idea of many small things.
items.exampleCN: 复数保留了「许多小东西」的意思。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「琐碎；琐事」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「微不足道地」
由该形容词加动词尾构成，义为「使显得琐碎」
由「使显得琐碎」加名词尾构成，义为「淡化；琐碎化」
由拉丁语「三岔路」构成，义为中世纪三门基础学科

definition_zh: 部队；一群；成群结队地走；军队
definition_en: a group of soldiers, or a group of people or animals moving together
core_image: 一队人排着走，脚步一同落下，扬起一小片尘土
scene: 清晨的操场上，一排士兵沿着跑道走成一列，背囊轻轻晃动。The troop moved slowly along the ridge at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 troop 是「部队、一队士兵」（第 1 个义项：成队行动的军人）；句意为部队在黎明时沿山脊缓缓行进。整齐同行的一队人正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 名词加 -er 构成，义为「骑兵；州警」
现在分词名词化，义为「列队行进」
合成词，义为「运兵车；运兵舰」

senses.title: A group of soldiers
senses.definition: a group of soldiers, especially a unit of cavalry or a body of troops in action
senses.definitionCN: 一队士兵，尤指骑兵单位或行动中的队伍
senses.example: The troop was ordered back to the base.
senses.exampleCN: 这支部队被命令返回基地。
senses.why: A troop is first a small body of riders, and the word keeps that picture of a band moving as one.
senses.whyCN: troop 最初指一小队骑手，这个词始终保留「一伙人走成一体」的画面。

senses.title: Soldiers in general
senses.definition: soldiers considered as a body, especially those sent to a place
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体的士兵，尤指派往某地的兵力
senses.example: Troops were sent to the border.
senses.exampleCN: 部队被派往边境。
senses.why: The plural widens the single unit into the whole body of soldiers on a front.
senses.whyCN: 复数把单个单位扩展成前线上的全部兵力。

senses.title: A group of people or animals
senses.definition: a group of people or animals moving together
senses.definitionCN: 一起行动的一群人或一群动物
senses.example: A troop of schoolchildren crossed the square.
senses.exampleCN: 一群小学生穿过广场。
senses.why: A band of soldiers is a band, and any other band moving together borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 一队士兵本就是一伙人，其他成伙走动的也用这个名字。

senses.title: To move in a group
senses.definition: to walk somewhere in a group, often without much order
senses.definitionCN: 成群地往某处走，常显得杂乱
senses.example: The children trooped into the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们成群地涌进礼堂。
senses.why: The verb is the noun set in motion: a troop walking becomes to troop.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是让名词走起来：一队人走路就成了 troop。

senses.title: A cavalry unit in the army
senses.definition: a small mounted or armoured unit forming part of a squadron or battalion
senses.definitionCN: 骑兵或装甲部队里的小单位，属中队或营建制
senses.example: The troop formed up at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 这个骑兵连在门口集合。
senses.why: Military organisation keeps the oldest sense, a small body of riders.
senses.whyCN: 军队编制保留了最古老的义项：一小队骑手。

intro.en: The word comes from French troupe, a band or company, and is probably of Germanic origin.
intro.cn: 这个词来自法语 troupe（一伙、一队），大概源出日耳曼语。

items.en: Troupe means a band, a company, or a crowd, and is used of soldiers and of players.
items.cn: 法语 troupe 意为一伙、一队、一群人，既用于士兵也用于演员。

items.en: The French word probably goes back to a Germanic root meaning a crowd or a herd.
items.cn: 这个法语词可能追溯到日耳曼语里表示人群或畜群词根。

items.en: English borrows it in the sixteenth century for a body of soldiers.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，指一队士兵。

items.en: The plural troops becomes the ordinary word for soldiers sent to a place.
items.cn: 其复数 troops 成了「派往某地的兵力」的通常说法。

items.en: The word also names a small cavalry unit and any group of animals or children.
items.cn: 这个词也指小型骑兵单位，以及任何一群动物或孩子。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the troupe spelling family, while the near-meaning group gathers other words for armed bodies and groups.
note.cn: 形近组同属 troupe 拼写家族，近义组汇集其他军队与群体的说法。

entries.definition: a company of actors or performers

entries.definition: a soldier in a cavalry or armoured unit
entries.definitionCN: 骑兵；州警

entries.definition: a curved shape closing on itself
entries.definitionCN: 环；圈

entries.definition: a prize won in a contest

entries.definition: the whole military force of a country

entries.definition: a small organised part of an army

entries.definition: a large number of people together
entries.definitionCN: 人群

entries.definition: a group of animals feeding or moving together
entries.definitionCN: 畜群

normalIntro.en: Troop and troupe are the same word split two ways: soldiers and players.
normalIntro.cn: troop 与 troupe 是同一个词的两条路：一边是兵，一边是演员。

normal.en: The plural troops is the everyday word for soldiers abroad.
normal.cn: 复数 troops 是「驻外部队」的日常说法。

normal.en: A trooper is the soldier in the troop.
normal.cn: trooper 就是队伍里的兵。

normal.en: Troupe keeps the French spelling for a company of actors.
normal.cn: troupe 保留法语拼法，指剧团。

normal.en: The verb usually goes with into or out of: they trooped out.
normal.cn: 动词常与 into 或 out of 连用：他们成群走出。

normal.en: A troop of monkeys works the same way as a troop of soldiers.
normal.cn: 一群猴子与一队士兵的用法相同。

abstract.en: Picture a line of soldiers walking a ridge at first light.
abstract.cn: 想象天刚亮时一列士兵走在山脊上。

abstract.en: Hear the boots land almost together.
abstract.cn: 听靴子几乎同时落地。

abstract.en: Then see a class of children do exactly the same on a stair.
abstract.cn: 再看一班孩子在同一段楼梯上做同样的动作。

examples.en: Fresh troops arrived at the front before winter.
examples.cn: 入冬前新部队抵达前线。

examples.en: A troop of monkeys crossed the road in single file.
examples.cn: 一群猴子排成一列过了马路。

examples.en: After the bell, the class trooped out into the yard.
examples.cn: 铃响后，全班成群涌到院子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「出普」——一出营门就排成普普通通的一队人。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense names a body of beings moving together, from cavalry to schoolchildren.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都指一起行动的一群，从骑兵到小学生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: boots landing almost together along a ridge.
core.cn: 核心意象：靴子几乎同时落在山脊上。

branches.en: The soldier senses, where a small unit is meant.
branches.cn: 士兵义：指的是具体的小单位。

branches.en: The force sense, where the plural means all the soldiers there.
branches.cn: 兵力义：复数指当地全部士兵。

branches.en: The group sense, where children or animals form the band.
branches.cn: 群体义：孩子或动物组成这一伙。

branches.en: The verb sense, where the band starts walking.
branches.cn: 动词义：这一伙动起来了。

branches.en: The unit sense again, where the formation is what counts.
branches.cn: 再回单位义：关键在队形。

intro.en: The word is French in shape, and the family around it is small and concrete.
intro.cn: 这个词带法语形状，周围的词族小而具体。
