definition_zh: 回归线；热带地区；（古）转折点
definition_en: either of the two parallels of latitude where the sun stands directly overhead at the solstice
core_image: 太阳在天空缓缓北移，到达一条界线后停住并折返，那条界线就是回归线
scene: 课本上的图示标出太阳直射点折返的那条界线。The diagram marks the Tropic of Cancer, where the noon sun stands overhead in June and then turns back.
sceneCN: 这里 tropic 指「太阳在夏至正午直射并随后折返的纬线」（第 1 个义项：北回归线）；句意为示意图标出北回归线，六月正午太阳在此当顶，随后转向南移。图中可辨识物件：地球、太阳光线、回归线、箭头。

derivatives.zh: 热带的；回归线的
在热带地区地
热带地区
向性；趋性
亚热带的

senses.title: The Tropic of Cancer
senses.titleCN: 北回归线：太阳北移的极限纬线
senses.definition: the northern parallel at about twenty-three and a half degrees north, where the sun is overhead at the June solstice
senses.definitionCN: 约北纬二十三度半、夏至时太阳直射的纬线
senses.example: The Tropic of Cancer crosses the Sahara and southern China.
senses.exampleCN: 北回归线穿过撒哈拉与中国南方。
senses.why: Greek trope 'a turn' names the line where the sun turns back; the northern one is named for the sign the sun entered.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 trope「转折」命名太阳折返之处；北面那条因太阳进入的星座而得名。

senses.title: The Tropic of Capricorn
senses.titleCN: 南回归线：太阳南移的极限纬线
senses.definition: the southern parallel at about twenty-three and a half degrees south, where the sun is overhead at the December solstice
senses.definitionCN: 约南纬二十三度半、冬至时太阳直射的纬线
senses.example: The Tropic of Capricorn runs through Australia and southern Africa.
senses.exampleCN: 南回归线穿过澳大利亚与非洲南部。
senses.why: The southern line is the same turn seen from the other hemisphere, named for the sign the sun enters in December.
senses.whyCN: 南面这条线是从另一半球看到的同一次折返，因太阳十二月进入的星座而得名。

senses.title: The tropics as a region
senses.titleCN: 热带地区：南北回归线之间的地带
senses.definition: the region of the earth between the two tropics
senses.definitionCN: 地球上两条回归线之间的地带
senses.example: Coffee and bananas grow throughout the tropics.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡与香蕉在整个热带地区都有种植。
senses.why: The two lines bound a belt, and the plural name of the lines became the name of the belt.
senses.whyCN: 两条线围出一条带，线的复数名称就成了这条带的名称。

senses.title: Tropical, as an attributive adjective
senses.titleCN: 热带的：作定语的形容词用法
senses.definition: relating to the tropics, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 与热带有关的，用于名词前
senses.example: Tropic heat and moisture favour dense forest.
senses.exampleCN: 热带的炎热与湿润有利于密林生长。
senses.why: English often uses the shorter tropic before a noun where tropical would also fit, a clipped attributive use.
senses.whyCN: 英语在名词前常用较短的 tropic，而 tropical 同样适用，这是截短的定语用法。

senses.title: The celestial tropic
senses.titleCN: 天球回归线：太阳在天球上的折返圈
senses.definition: either of the two circles on the celestial sphere marking the sun's greatest declination
senses.definitionCN: 天球上标出太阳最大赤纬的两条圈之一
senses.example: The celestial tropic touches the ecliptic at the solstice points.
senses.exampleCN: 天球回归线在二至点与黄道相切。
senses.why: The sky repeats the terrestrial limit in its own circles, marking where the sun's declination stops.
senses.whyCN: 天空用它自己的圈重复地表的界限，标出太阳赤纬停止之处。

senses.title: A turning point, archaic
senses.titleCN: 转折点：事情转向的时刻（古义）
senses.definition: a point of turning or change, the older general sense of the Greek root
senses.definitionCN: 转向或改变的时刻，即希腊词根的较早一般义
senses.example: The old text speaks of the tropic of fortune.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇旧文谈到命运的转折点。
senses.why: The root's general sense of turning survives in older writing about any change of course.
senses.whyCN: 词根的一般「转向」义在谈论任何路线改变的旧文字中留存。

senses.title: A tropic response in biology
senses.titleCN: 向性的：生物对刺激转向的反应
senses.definition: describing a movement or growth directed by a stimulus such as light or gravity
senses.definitionCN: 描述由光、重力等刺激引导的运动或生长
senses.example: Roots show a tropic response to gravity.
senses.exampleCN: 根对重力表现出向性反应。
senses.why: A plant organ turns toward or away from a stimulus, which is the root's literal 'turn' applied to growth.
senses.whyCN: 植物器官朝刺激转向或背离，正是词根字面的「转」用于生长。

senses.title: The torrid zone between the tropics
senses.titleCN: 热带地带：两回归线之间的气候带
senses.definition: the hot climate belt lying between the two tropics
senses.definitionCN: 位于两条回归线之间的炎热气候带
senses.example: The torrid zone receives the sun almost vertically all year.
senses.exampleCN: 热带地带全年几乎接受垂直照射的阳光。
senses.why: The belt between the lines stays hot because the sun remains high there throughout the year.
senses.whyCN: 两线之间的地带之所以炎热，是因为太阳全年都保持在较高位置。

intro.en: Tropic comes from Latin tropicus, from Greek tropikos 'of a turn, of the solstice', built on trope 'a turn' and trepein 'to turn'. The lines are named for the sun's turning at the solstices. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: tropic 来自拉丁 tropicus，源于希腊 tropikos「转折的、至点的」，由 trope「转折」与 trepein「转动」构成；这两条线因太阳在二至点折返而得名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trope meant 'a turn, a turning', especially of the sun or of a argument.
items.cn: trope 意为「转折、转向」，尤指太阳的折返或论证的转折。

items.en: Trepein meant 'to turn'. The noun and verb form one of the most productive roots in Greek.
items.cn: trepein 意为「转动」。这个名词与动词构成希腊语中最多产的词根之一。

items.en: Tropikos meant 'of a turn', and in astronomy 'of the solstice', because the sun appears to turn back there.
items.cn: tropikos 意为「转折的」，在天文学中指「至点的」，因为太阳在那里看似折返。

items.en: Latin borrowed the adjective as tropicus; the noun tropicus circulus named the solstitial circle.
items.cn: 拉丁把这个形容词借作 tropicus；名词短语 tropicus circulus 指至点圈。

items.en: English tropic appears in the sixteenth century for the two solstitial parallels, and the plural tropics soon named the belt between them.
items.cn: 英语 tropic 在 16 世纪出现，指两条至点纬线；复数 the tropics 很快指它们之间的地带。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): the biological 'tropic response' sense and the archaic 'turning point' sense have no precisely dated first English use; the Greek root is not in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：生物学的「向性反应」义与古义「转折点」在英语中的确切首见年代未见记录；希腊词根则无争议。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound like tropic; group two holds the lines and belts it belongs to.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近 tropic 的词；第二组是它所归属的线与地带。

entries.definition: A subject of discussion, from Greek ta topika 'things about places'; it is not related to turning.
entries.definitionCN: 讨论的主题，来自希腊 ta topika「关于处所之事」；与「转动」无关。

entries.definition: A prize or memorial, from Greek tropaion 'a rout of the enemy'; the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 奖品或纪念物，来自希腊 tropaion「击溃敌人」；词根不同。

entries.definition: A directed growth response to a stimulus, built on the same Greek trope 'turn'.
entries.definitionCN: 对刺激的有方向生长反应，同出希腊 trope「转」。

entries.definition: A figurative turn of phrase, literally a 'turning' of meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 比喻性的说法，字面就是意义的「转向」。

entries.definition: The zero-latitude circle halfway between the tropics, where day and night are equal.
entries.definitionCN: 两条回归线正中的零度纬线，那里昼夜等长。

entries.definition: Angular distance from the equator; the tropics are two particular latitudes.
entries.definitionCN: 相对赤道的角距离；回归线是两个特定的纬度。

entries.definition: Any circle parallel to the equator; a tropic is one named parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 与赤道平行的任一圈；回归线是其中有名的一条。

entries.definition: The two times of year when the sun reaches its greatest declination and turns back.
entries.definitionCN: 一年中太阳到达最大赤纬并折返的两个时刻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Greek 'turn', real solstice astronomy and real geography, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊「转」、真实的至点天文与真实地理，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Trope 'a turn' + -ic: the line where the sun turns back at the solstice.
normal.cn: trope「转折」+ -ic：太阳在至点折返的那条线。

normal.en: The Tropic of Cancer is northern; the Tropic of Capricorn is southern.
normal.cn: 北回归线在北，南回归线在南。

normal.en: The tropics lie between the two tropics and are hot all year.
normal.cn: the tropics 位于两条回归线之间，全年炎热。

normal.en: The same Greek root gives tropism, a plant's turning response to light.
normal.cn: 同一希腊词根衍生 tropism，即植物对光的转向反应。

normal.en: Celestial tropics mark the sun's greatest declination on the sky.
normal.cn: 天球回归线标出太阳在天球上的最大赤纬。

abstract.en: Picture a pendulum that swings north and stops just before returning.
abstract.cn: 想象一只向北摆动的摆锤，在返回前停住。

abstract.en: Picture a path with two marked fences, beyond which the sun never goes overhead.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路两侧各有一道标线，太阳从不越过它们当顶。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that changes direction at a single sharp word.
abstract.cn: 想象一场对话在一个尖刻的词上突然转向。

examples.en: The Tropic of Cancer passes through the northern hemisphere.
examples.cn: 北回归线穿过北半球。

examples.en: Rainforests cover much of the tropics.
examples.cn: 雨林覆盖了热带地区的大部分。

examples.en: The sun stands overhead at the tropic on the solstice.
examples.cn: 至点时太阳在回归线上当顶。

dict_mnemonic.text: trop（转，如 trope 转义）+ ic → 太阳折返的线 → 回归线、热带

root: 希腊 tropikos「转折的、至点的」= trope「转折」+ -ikos；源于 trepein「转动」，指太阳在二至点折返的纬线。拉丁 tropicus，英语 16 世纪借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses revolve around one turn: the two solstitial parallels where the sun reverses, the belt they enclose, the attributive use, the sky's corresponding circles, the old 'turning point', the biological turning response, and the hot zone itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一次「折返」：太阳转向的两条至点纬线、它们围出的地带、定语用法、天空中的对应圈、古义「转折点」、生物学的转向反应，以及炎热地带本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sun moving north or south, reaching a marked line, and turning back.
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳向北或向南移动，到达一条标线后折返。

branches.en: TWO LIMITS: the northern and southern parallels mark the two ends of the sun's yearly swing.
branches.cn: 两条界线：南北两条纬线标出太阳一年摆动的两端。

branches.en: THE BELT: the space between the lines becomes a hot region and a climate zone.
branches.cn: 地带：两线之间的空间成为炎热地区与气候带。

branches.en: ATTRIBUTIVE: the short form works before a noun as a clipped adjective.
branches.cn: 定语：较短形式可在名词前作截短形容词。

branches.en: SKY: the celestial tropics mirror the earthly limits on the celestial sphere.
branches.cn: 天空：天球回归线在天球上镜像地表的界限。

branches.en: TURNING: the old sense names any turning point, and biology names a growth response that turns toward a stimulus.
branches.cn: 转折：古义指任何转折点，生物学则指朝刺激转向的生长反应。

intro.en: Tropic is an adjective from Greek 'turn'; its family includes tropical, tropism and trope, all built on the same root.
intro.cn: tropic 是来自希腊「转」的形容词；其词族包括 tropical、tropism 与 trope，均建于同一词根。

latinIntro.en: Greek trope 'a turn' and trepein 'to turn' give tropikos, Latin tropicus and English tropic; the same root yields tropical and tropism, while trophy comes from a different Greek branch, tropaion 'a rout'.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 trope「转折」与 trepein「转动」衍生 tropikos、拉丁 tropicus 与英语 tropic；同一词根还衍生 tropical 与 tropism，而 trophy 来自另一支希腊词 tropaion「击溃」。

items.example: The verb supplies the action of turning.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供「转动」的动作。

items.example: A trope in rhetoric is a turn of meaning.
items.exampleCN: 修辞中的 trope 是意义的转向。

items.meaning: of a turn; of the solstice
items.example: The adjective named the solstitial circle.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词命名至点圈。

items.example: Latin kept the Greek meaning.

items.example: The Tropic of Cancer marks the northern limit.
items.exampleCN: 北回归线标出北界。

items.example: Tropical forests are humid all year.
items.exampleCN: 热带森林全年湿润。

items.example: The tropics receive heavy rain.
items.exampleCN: 热带地区降雨丰沛。

items.example: Phototropism bends a shoot toward light.
items.exampleCN: 向光性使幼苗朝光弯曲。

definition_zh: 热带的；炎热的（如热带般闷热的）
definition_en: belonging to the hot regions near the equator, or as hot and humid as those regions
core_image: 雨林里巨大的叶片垂着水珠，藤蔓从高树一直挂下来
scene: 雨林的午后，空气闷得像浸过水，宽大的叶子仍在滴水。The garden is full of tropical plants from South America.
sceneCN: 这里 tropical 是「热带的」（第 1 个义项：属于赤道附近炎热地区的）；句意为园中满是来自南美的热带植物。雨林里滴水的大叶和藤蔓，就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 由 tropical 去掉后缀构成，义为「热带地区」
tropical 的词根名词，义为「回归线；热带」
由 sub-（副）与 tropical 复合，义为「亚热带的」

senses.title: Near the equator
senses.definition: belonging to the belt of the earth that lies near the equator and is always warm
senses.definitionCN: 属于地球赤道附近终年温暖的那一带
senses.example: The garden is full of tropical plants from South America.
senses.exampleCN: 园中满是来自南美的热带植物。
senses.why: Greek tropos, a turn, named the line where the sun turns back, and the whole belt took that name.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 tropos（转向）命名了太阳折返的那条线，整条地带也随之得名。

senses.title: Weather that feels like it
senses.definition: used of weather that is hot and damp even far from the equator
senses.definitionCN: 形容即使远离赤道也又热又潮的天气
senses.example: The air was tropical for a week after the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后有一周空气都闷热得像热带。
senses.why: A heat that hangs and does not dry out copies the feeling of the equator, so any such day may be called tropical.
senses.whyCN: 那种悬着不散的湿热复制了赤道的感觉，于是这样的日子也被称作 tropical。

intro.en: Tropical belongs to the noun tropic, which comes from the Greek tropos, a turn, because the sun appears to turn back at the tropics.
intro.cn: tropical 属于名词 tropic，后者来自希腊语 tropos（转向），因为太阳在回归线处看起来折返。

items.en: Tropos meant a turn or a way of turning, from trepein, to turn.
items.cn: tropos 意为转向或转向的方式，出自 trepein（转）。

items.en: The adjective tropicus was used of the solstice, the sun's turning point.
items.cn: 形容词 tropicus 原用于至日，即太阳折返的时刻。

items.en: The two tropics were named as the lines where the sun turns back each year.
items.cn: 两条回归线得名于太阳每年折返之处。

items.en: English tropic named the lines, and tropical described the whole hot belt between them.
items.cn: 英语用 tropic 指这两条线，tropical 形容它们之间整条炎热的地带。

items.en: The word then extended to hot, damp weather anywhere and to storms born in that belt.
items.cn: 这个词进而扩展指任何地方的湿热天气与诞生于该地带的风暴。

note.en: The first group shares the trop stem, the second holds other words for heat and climate zones.
note.cn: 第一组共享 trop 词干，第二组收其他表示炎热与气候区的词。

entries.definitionCN: 热带地区

entries.definition: Either of the two turning lines of the sun.
entries.definitionCN: 回归线

entries.definition: Just outside the tropics.
entries.definitionCN: 亚热带的

entries.definition: Of the line around the middle of the earth.
entries.definitionCN: 赤道的

entries.definition: Hot and damp in a heavy way.
entries.definitionCN: 闷热的；湿热的

entries.definition: Carrying a lot of water in the air.
entries.definitionCN: 潮湿的

normalIntro.en: Tropical is tropic plus -al, and tropic comes from a word for turning, because the sun turns back at those lines.
normalIntro.cn: tropical 是 tropic 加 -al，而 tropic 出自表示「转」的词，因为太阳在那些线上折返。

normal.en: Trop means turn, so the tropics are where the sun turns back.
normal.cn: trop 意为转，所以热带是太阳折返的地方。

normal.en: The adjective simply adds -al to tropic.
normal.cn: 形容词只是在 tropic 后加 -al。

normal.en: The tropics is always plural for the region itself.
normal.cn: 指整个地区时 tropics 总是复数。

normal.en: Sub in front gives subtropical, just outside the belt.
normal.cn: 前面加 sub 得 subtropical，就在那带之外。

normal.en: Tropical fish live in warm water, not in the sea of the far north.
normal.cn: tropical fish 生活在温暖的水里，不在北方远海。

abstract.en: A leaf so large it holds a small pool.
abstract.cn: 一片大得能盛一小池水的叶子。

abstract.en: Air that feels like warm wet cloth on the face.
abstract.cn: 像热湿布贴在脸上的空气。

abstract.en: Vines hanging straight down from the high canopy.
abstract.cn: 藤蔓从高处树冠笔直垂下。

examples.en: Tropical rainforests hold more species than any other place on land.
examples.cn: 热带雨林所含物种比陆地上任何地方都多。

examples.en: Bananas and mangoes are examples of tropical fruit.
examples.cn: 香蕉和芒果都是热带水果。

examples.en: The coast was hit by a tropical storm in August.
examples.cn: 海岸在八月遭到一场热带风暴袭击。

dict_mnemonic.text: trop（转）＋ ical——太阳在这里折返，所以终年炎热，就是热带的。

root: 由 tropic 加 -al 构成，源自希腊语 tropē、tropos（转向）与拉丁语 tropicus，本指太阳折返的至日与回归线，后指其间炎热地带；同族词有 tropics、tropic、subtropical。

sensesIntro.en: First the belt near the equator, then the heavy heat that feels like it.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是赤道附近那条地带，再是像那条地带一样的闷热。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dripping leaf in the rainforest.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨林里滴水的宽叶。

branches.en: The geography branch: plants and animals of the belt.
branches.cn: 地理分支：那条地带的动植物。

branches.en: The weather branch: heat that hangs and will not dry.
branches.cn: 天气分支：悬着不散的湿热。

branches.en: The sunlight branch: both come from a high warm sun.
branches.cn: 阳光分支：两者都来自高悬的暖阳。

branches.en: The storm branch: storms born over warm seas.
branches.cn: 风暴分支：出生在暖海上的风暴。

branches.en: The imagination branch: any day can feel tropical.
branches.cn: 想象分支：任何一天都能感觉像热带。

intro.en: Tropical joins the Greek stem trop, a turn, with the adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: tropical 把希腊词干 trop（转向）与形容词后缀 -al 结合起来。

latinIntro.en: The Greek root trepein, to turn, reached English through Latin tropicus, and the turning words below share it.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词根 trepein（转）经拉丁语 tropicus 进入英语，下面的「转」类词与它同源。

items.example: The stem explains the sun turning back.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干解释了太阳的折返。

items.example: It forms tropic, of the turning line.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 tropic，与回归线有关的。

items.example: It forms tropical from tropic.
items.exampleCN: 它由 tropic 构成 tropical。

items.example: The region takes a plural name.
items.exampleCN: 这个地区用复数命名。

items.example: Sub marks a zone just outside.
items.exampleCN: sub 标出紧邻在外的一带。

items.example: The adjective describes weather and life.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述天气与生物。

items.example: A plant turns toward light by tropism.
items.exampleCN: 植物靠向性转向光。

items.meaning: a prize for a turning of fortune
items.example: The old root also underlies the word for a prize.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老词根也支撑着表示奖品的词。

latinEntries.meaning: of the turning of the sun

definition_zh: 麻烦的；令人烦恼的；棘手的；讨厌的
definition_en: causing trouble, difficulty, or annoyance
core_image: 一扇门关不严，风一吹就咯咯响，怎么修都不服帖
scene: 课堂上，后排两个学生一直传纸条，老师几次停下来看他们。The troublesome noise from the pipes kept the whole floor awake.
sceneCN: 这里 troublesome 是「令人烦恼的」（第 1 个义项：带来麻烦、令人不快）；句意为管道传来的恼人噪声让整层楼都睡不着。关不严的门反复作响正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：麻烦的；令人烦恼的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「麻烦地；令人烦恼地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「麻烦；棘手」
去掉 -some 的基础名词，义为「麻烦」

senses.title: Causing annoyance
senses.definition: causing annoyance or difficulty, especially again and again
senses.definitionCN: 反复带来烦恼或困难
senses.example: The troublesome tap drips all night.
senses.exampleCN: 那个讨厌的水龙头滴了一整夜。
senses.why: The suffix -some means causing, so the word says plainly that trouble is being caused.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -some 意为「引起」，所以这个词直说：麻烦正在被引起。

senses.title: Hard to deal with
senses.definition: difficult to handle, solve, or control
senses.definitionCN: 难以处理、解决或控制的
senses.example: The border issue is a troublesome one.
senses.exampleCN: 边境问题是个棘手的问题。
senses.why: A problem earns the suffix when every solution costs more than it seems worth.
senses.whyCN: 一道难题一旦每个解法都代价高过所值，就配上了这个词尾。

senses.title: Behaving badly
senses.definition: of a person, often behaving badly and causing work for others
senses.definitionCN: 指人常常胡闹、给别人添事
senses.example: He was a troublesome pupil in his first year.
senses.exampleCN: 他第一年是个难管的学生。
senses.why: A person who keeps causing work is someone who keeps causing trouble, so -some fits again.
senses.whyCN: 常给人添活的人就是常惹麻烦的人，所以 -some 依然合适。

intro.en: The word is English through and through: the noun trouble plus the suffix -some, causing.
intro.cn: 这个词彻头彻尾是英语自造：名词 trouble 加上意为「引起」的后缀 -some。

items.en: Troubler supplies the base noun and verb, meaning to disturb.
items.cn: 古法语 troubler 提供了基础名词与动词，意为扰乱。

items.en: The noun trouble is in use by the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 trouble 在十三世纪已在使用。

items.en: The suffix -some forms adjectives from nouns, as in handsome and tiresome.
items.cn: 后缀 -some 由名词构成形容词，如 handsome 与 tiresome。

items.en: Troublesome is recorded from the sixteenth century with the sense of causing trouble.
items.cn: troublesome 从十六世纪起有记录，意为引起麻烦。

items.en: It now covers things, times, and people that are hard to manage.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖难对付的事物、时期与人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other -some adjectives, while the near-meaning group names other words for annoying things.
note.cn: 形近组汇集其他 -some 形容词，近义组列出其他表示恼人的词。

entries.definitionCN: 麻烦；困难

entries.definition: making you feel tired and bored
entries.definitionCN: 令人厌烦的

entries.definition: causing slight annoyance
entries.definitionCN: 让人心烦的

entries.definition: good looking; the suffix is shared, the meaning differs
entries.definitionCN: 英俊的；只是词尾相同，意思不同

entries.definition: making you feel slightly angry

entries.definition: causing no damage or trouble
entries.definitionCN: 无害的；无碍的

normalIntro.en: Trouble plus -some, and -some always means causing.
normalIntro.cn: trouble 加 -some，而 -some 总是表示「引起」。

normal.en: Tiresome, bothersome, and troublesome share one suffix.
normal.cn: tiresome、bothersome、troublesome 共用同一个词尾。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable: TROUB-lesome.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节：TROUB-lesome。

normal.en: The adverb adds -ly and the noun adds -ness.
normal.cn: 副词加 -ly，名词加 -ness。

normal.en: The word can describe things, times, and people alike.
normal.cn: 这个词既可形容事物、时期，也可形容人。

normal.en: Its base noun takes no article when used in the abstract.
normal.cn: 作抽象用法时，它的基础名词不带冠词。

abstract.en: Picture a door that will not shut properly.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇怎么也关不严的门。

abstract.en: Hear it rattle whenever the wind comes past.
abstract.cn: 听风一过就咯咯作响。

abstract.en: Feel how that sound keeps nagging at the ear.
abstract.cn: 体会那声音怎样一直磨着耳朵。

examples.en: The cough proved more troublesome than the fever.
examples.cn: 咳嗽比发烧更让人难受。

examples.en: They found the tax rules particularly troublesome.
examples.cn: 他们发现税务规定特别棘手。

examples.en: A troublesome cough kept him off work for a week.
examples.cn: 一场讨厌的咳嗽让他一周没能上班。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「穿了不松」——鞋穿了不松，却磨脚磨得烦人。

root: trouble（拉丁语 turba「骚动」经古法语）+ 后缀 -some（引起……的），英语自造词

sensesIntro.en: The suffix links all three senses: whatever or whoever keeps causing trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: 词尾把三个义项串起来：凡是不停引起麻烦的东西或人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door that will not shut and rattles in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇关不严的门，风里咯咯作响。

branches.en: The annoyance sense, where the trouble is a sound or a fault.
branches.cn: 烦人义：麻烦是声音或毛病。

branches.en: The difficult sense, where the trouble is a problem.
branches.cn: 棘手义：麻烦是一道难题。

branches.en: The personal sense, where the trouble is a person.
branches.cn: 人事义：麻烦来自一个人。

branches.en: The mixture, where a fault becomes a problem for everyone.
branches.cn: 混合义：小毛病成了大家的难题。

branches.en: The plain annoyance sense again, where the rattle goes on.
branches.cn: 再回烦人义：那响声还在继续。

intro.en: The word is a native compound, built from a French noun and an English suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词是本土合成，由一个法语名词加一个英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The base trouble goes back to Latin turba, so the Latin list gives that root.
latinIntro.cn: 它的基础词 trouble 上溯到拉丁语 turba，故拉丁同源词列出这个词根。

items.example: Trouble gives troublesome.
items.exampleCN: trouble 加它成为 troublesome。

items.example: It was a tiresome wait.
items.exampleCN: 那是一场令人厌烦的等待。

items.example: The flies were bothersome.
items.exampleCN: 苍蝇实在烦人。

items.example: He was a handsome young man.
items.exampleCN: 他是个英俊的年轻人。

items.exampleCN: 麻烦来得毫无预兆。

items.example: Troublesome gives troublesomely.
items.exampleCN: troublesome 加它成为 troublesomely。

items.example: Troublesome gives troublesomeness.
items.exampleCN: troublesome 加它成为 troublesomeness。

items.example: Wholesome food is not always plain.
items.exampleCN: 健康食物未必寡淡。

items.example: The storm was fearsome.
items.exampleCN: 那场暴风雨很可怕。
